title.zh: 卷一百二十二 列傳第九: 巴而朮阿而忒的斤 鐵邁赤 按扎兒 雪不台 唵木海 昔里鈐部 槊直腯魯華 昔兒吉思 哈散納
title.en: Volume 122 Biographies 9: Baurchuk Art Tekin, Tiemaichi, Anzha'er, Xuebutai, Anmuhai, Xiliqianbu, Shuozhituluhua, Xi'erjisi, Hasanna
title.raw: 卷一百二十二 列傳第九: 巴而朮阿而忒的斤 鐵邁赤 按扎兒 雪不台 唵木海 昔里鈐部 槊直腯魯華 昔兒吉思 哈散納 Volume 122 Biographies 9: Baurchuk Art Tekin, Tiemaichi, Anzha'er, Xuebutai, Anmuhai, Xiliqianbu, Shuozhituluhua, Xi'erjisi, Hasanna

sentences.zh: 巴而術阿而忒的斤

translations.literal: Baurchuk Art Tekin
translations.idiomatic: Baurchuk Art Tekin

sentences.zh: 巴而術阿而忒的斤亦都護，亦都護者，高昌國主號也。

translations.literal: Baurchuk Art Tekin was Idiqut; Idiqut is the title of the lord of the Gaochang state.
translations.idiomatic: Baurchuk Art Tekin held the title of Idiqut—the designation borne by rulers of Gaochang.

sentences.zh: 先世居畏兀兒之地，有和林山，二水出焉，曰禿忽剌，曰薛靈哥。

translations.literal: Ancestral generations dwelt in the land of the Uyghurs; there was Mount Khoshut, and two waters issued from it, called Toghulqa and called Xilingge.
translations.idiomatic: His forebears had long lived in Uyghur country, where Mount Khoshut stood; two rivers rose there, the Toghulqa and the Xilingge.

sentences.zh: 一夕，有神光降於樹，在兩河之間，人即其所而候之，樹乃生癭，若懷妊狀，自是光常見。

translations.literal: One evening divine light descended upon a tree between the two rivers; people went to that place to wait upon it; the tree then produced a knob as if in pregnancy; from this the light was often seen.
translations.idiomatic: One night a supernatural radiance settled on a tree between the two rivers. People gathered there to watch, and the trunk swelled as though with child; thereafter the light appeared again and again.

sentences.zh: 越九月又十日，而樹癭裂，得嬰兒者五，土人收養之。

translations.literal: After nine months and again ten days the tree's knob split open; five infant children were obtained, and the natives reared them.
translations.idiomatic: Nine months and ten days later the swelling split apart, yielding five infants whom the local people took in and raised.

sentences.zh: 其最稚者曰不古可罕。

translations.literal: The youngest of them was called Bögü Qaghan.
translations.idiomatic: The youngest they named Bögü Qaghan.

sentences.zh: 既壯，遂能有其民人土田，而為之君長。

translations.literal: When he had grown strong, he was then able to possess their people, lands, and soil, and became their chieftain.
translations.idiomatic: Once he came of age, he won control of their people and territory and became their ruler.

sentences.zh: 傳三十餘君，是為玉倫的斤，數與唐人相攻戰，久之議和親，以息民罷兵。

translations.literal: Passing down through more than thirty lords, this was Yulümdüjin, who several times attacked and fought with the Tang people; after a long time they discussed marriage alliance to rest the people and cease troops.
translations.idiomatic: After more than thirty generations the line reached Yulümdüjin, who waged repeated war against the Tang. At length the two sides agreed to a marriage alliance so the people might rest and the armies stand down.

sentences.zh: 於是唐以金蓮公主妻的斤之子葛勵的斤，居和林別力跛力答，言婦所居山也。

translations.literal: Thereupon the Tang gave the Golden Lotus Princess in marriage to Yulümdüjin's son Külijin, dwelling at Khoshut at Belipulida, meaning the mountain where the woman dwelt.
translations.idiomatic: The Tang then married the Golden Lotus Princess to Külijin, Yulümdüjin's son, who resided at Khoshut on Belipulida—the name of the mountain where his wife lived.

sentences.zh: 又有山曰天哥裏於答哈，言天靈山也。

translations.literal: There was also a mountain called Tiangeriyüdaha, meaning Heavenly Spirit Mountain.
translations.idiomatic: There was another peak called Tiangeriyüdaha, "Mountain of the Heavenly Spirit."

sentences.zh: 南有石山曰胡力答哈，言福山也。

translations.literal: To the south was a stone mountain called Hulidaha, meaning Fortune Mountain.
translations.idiomatic: South of it stood a stony hill named Hulidaha, "Mountain of Blessing."

sentences.zh: 唐使與相地者至其國，曰：「和林之盛強，以有此山也。

translations.literal: Tang envoys who came to survey the land with them arrived in their state and said: "Khoshut's strength and prosperity are due to having this mountain.
translations.idiomatic: When Tang envoys came to map the land with them, they declared, "Khoshut's power rests on this mountain.

sentences.zh: 盍壞其山，以弱其國？」

translations.literal: Why not destroy this mountain to weaken their state?"
translations.idiomatic: Why not demolish it and weaken the kingdom?"

sentences.zh: 乃告諸的斤曰：「既為婚姻，將有求於爾，其與之乎？

translations.literal: They thereupon told Yulümdüjin: "Now that we are joined by marriage, we shall have a request of you—will you grant it?
translations.idiomatic: They then said to Yulümdüjin, "We are kin by marriage now; we must ask something of you—will you give it?

sentences.zh: 福山之石，於上國無所用，而唐人願見。」

translations.literal: The stone of Fortune Mountain is of no use to the upper state, yet the Tang people wish to see it."
translations.idiomatic: The stone on Fortune Mountain is useless to our empire, but the Tang wish to take it away."

sentences.zh: 的斤遂與之石，大不能動，唐人以烈火焚之，沃以醲醋，其石碎，乃輦而去。

translations.literal: Yulümdüjin thereupon gave them the stone; it was so large it could not be moved; the Tang people burned it with fierce fire and poured thick vinegar upon it; the stone shattered, and they carried it away on carts.
translations.idiomatic: Yulümdüjin yielded the boulder, too massive to budge until the Tang heated it with fire and drenched it with strong vinegar, breaking it apart and hauling the pieces away.

sentences.zh: 國中鳥獸為之悲號。

translations.literal: Within the state birds and beasts wailed for it.
translations.idiomatic: Throughout the realm birds and beasts cried out in grief.

sentences.zh: 後七日，玉倫的斤卒，災異屢見，民弗安居，傳位者又數亡，乃遷於交州。

translations.literal: Seven days later Yulümdüjin died; calamities and prodigies were repeatedly seen; the people could not dwell in peace; those who received the succession also several times perished; they thereupon moved to Jiaozhou.
translations.idiomatic: Seven days later Yulümdüjin died. Omens and disasters multiplied, the people could not remain settled, and successive rulers died in turn, so the court relocated to Jiaozhou.

sentences.zh: 交州即火州也。

translations.literal: Jiaozhou is Huozhou.
translations.idiomatic: Jiaozhou is Huozhou (Fire Prefecture).

sentences.zh: 統別失八里之地，北至阿術河，南接酒泉，東至兀敦、甲石哈，西臨西蕃。

translations.literal: Ruling the territory of Beshbaligh, north to the Ashi River, south joining Jiuquan, east reaching Udun and Jiashige, west bordering the Western Barbarians.
translations.idiomatic: They governed Beshbaligh, reaching the Ashi River in the north, Jiuquan in the south, Udun and Jiashige in the east, and the western frontier peoples on the west.

sentences.zh: 居是者凡百七十餘載，而至巴而術阿而忒的斤，臣於契丹。

translations.literal: Those dwelling there altogether for more than one hundred seventy years, down to Baurchuk Art Tekin, who submitted to the Khitan.
translations.idiomatic: For some one hundred seventy years they held this land, until Baurchuk Art Tekin came to submit to the Khitan.

sentences.zh: 歲己巳，聞太祖興朔方，遂殺契丹所置監國等官，欲來附。

translations.literal: In the year jisi, hearing that the Founder was rising in the north, he thereupon killed the Khitan-appointed overseers and officials, intending to come and attach himself.
translations.idiomatic: In the jisi year (1209), learning that the Founder was advancing in the northern regions, he slew the officials the Khitan had posted to supervise his country and prepared to submit.

sentences.zh: 未行，帝遣使使其國。

translations.literal: Before he had set out, the Emperor sent envoys to his state.
translations.idiomatic: Before he could depart, the Emperor dispatched envoys to his realm.

sentences.zh: 亦都護大喜，即遣使入奏曰：「臣聞皇帝威德，即棄契丹舊好，方將通誠，不自意天使降臨下國，自今而後，願率部眾為臣仆。」

translations.literal: The Idiqut was greatly pleased and immediately sent envoys to enter a memorial saying: "Your subject has heard of the Emperor's majesty and virtue and has cast off the old friendship with Khitan; I was just about to offer sincerity when, beyond my expectation, the heavenly envoy descended upon my humble state—from this day forward I wish to lead my clansmen and followers as servants and slaves."
translations.idiomatic: The Idiqut was overjoyed and at once sent a memorial: "Having learned of Your Majesty's awe-inspiring virtue, I have broken with the Khitan. I was on the point of pledging loyalty when, unlooked-for, your heavenly envoy arrived in my petty realm. Henceforth I desire to lead my people as your subject and servant."

sentences.zh: 是時帝征大陽可汗，射其子脫脫殺之。

translations.literal: At that time the Emperor was campaigning against the Tayang Qaghan and shot and killed his son Toto.
translations.idiomatic: At that time the Emperor was campaigning against Tayang Qaghan and shot dead his son Toto.

sentences.zh: 脫脫之子火都、赤剌溫、馬劄兒、禿薛幹四人，以不能歸全屍，遂取其頭涉也兒的石河，將奔亦都護，先遣使往，亦都護殺之。

translations.literal: Toto's sons Hodu, Chilawen, Majar, and Tuxgan—the four men—because they could not recover the whole corpse, thereupon took his head and crossed the Yelüshi River, intending to flee to the Idiqut; they first sent envoys ahead, and the Idiqut killed them.
translations.idiomatic: Toto's sons Hodu, Chilawen, Majar, and Tuxgan, unable to recover his entire body, cut off his head and crossed the Yelüshi River, planning to flee to the Idiqut; they sent envoys ahead, and the Idiqut had those envoys killed.

sentences.zh: 四人者至，與大戰於襜河。

translations.literal: When the four men arrived, they fought a great battle on the Zhan River.
translations.idiomatic: When the four arrived, they fought a major battle on the Zhan River.

sentences.zh: 亦都護遣其國相來報，帝復遣使還諭亦都護，遂以金寶入貢。

translations.literal: The Idiqut sent his state chancellor to report; the Emperor again sent envoys back to instruct the Idiqut, and he thereupon presented gold and treasures in tribute.
translations.idiomatic: The Idiqut sent his chief minister with a report; the Emperor sent envoys in reply to confirm his allegiance, and the Idiqut then offered tribute in gold and precious goods.

sentences.zh: 辛未，朝帝於怯綠連河，奏曰：「陛下若恩顧臣，使臣得與陛下四子之末，庶幾竭其犬馬之力。」

translations.literal: In xinwei he attended the court at the Qielülian River and memorialized: "If Your Majesty will favor your subject with grace, granting that your subject may stand among the youngest of Your Majesty's four sons, I might exhaust the strength of dog and horse."
translations.idiomatic: In the xinwei year (1211) he attended court on the Qielülian River and said, "If Your Majesty will show me favor, placing me among the youngest of your four sons, I may then devote the strength of hound and horse."

sentences.zh: 帝感其言，使尚公主也立安敦，且得序於諸子。

translations.literal: The Emperor was moved by his words, made him marry the Princess Yilian Andun, and allowed him to be ordered among the sons.
translations.idiomatic: Moved by this speech, the Emperor married him to Princess Yilian Andun and ranked him with his sons.

sentences.zh: 與者必那演征罕勉力、鎖潭回回諸國，將部曲萬人以先。

translations.literal: Together with Zhebinayan he campaigned against Hanmianli, Suotan, and the Muslim states, leading ten thousand men of his command as vanguard.
translations.idiomatic: He marched with Zhebinayan against Hanmianli, Suotan, and the Muslim lands at the head of ten thousand of his troops.

sentences.zh: 紀律嚴明，所向克捷。

translations.literal: Discipline was strict and clear; wherever they turned they conquered.
translations.idiomatic: His discipline was strict, and wherever his forces turned they prevailed.

sentences.zh: 又從帝征你沙卜裏，征河西，皆有大功。

translations.literal: He also followed the Emperor in campaigns against Nishabur and the Hexi region, in all winning great merit.
translations.idiomatic: He also followed the Emperor in campaigns against Nishabur and in Hexi, winning great distinction in each.

sentences.zh: 既卒，而次子玉古倫赤的斤嗣。

translations.literal: When he died, his second son Yigulunchidijin succeeded.
translations.idiomatic: After his death his second son Yigulunchidijin succeeded him.

sentences.zh: 玉古倫赤的斤卒，子馬木剌的斤嗣。

translations.literal: When Yigulunchidijin died, his son Mamuladijin succeeded.
translations.idiomatic: When Yigulunchidijin died, his son Mamuladijin succeeded.

sentences.zh: 將探馬軍萬人，從憲宗伐宋合州，攻釣魚山有功，還火州卒。

translations.literal: He led ten thousand men of the scouting cavalry, followed Möngke Khan in attacking Hezhou in the Song campaign, stormed Diaoyu Mountain with merit, returned to Huozhou and died.
translations.idiomatic: Leading ten thousand scouting horsemen, he followed Möngke Khan against Song Hezhou, distinguished himself at the assault on Diaoyu Mountain, and died after returning to Huozhou.

sentences.zh: 至元三年，世祖命其子火赤哈兒的斤嗣為亦都護。

translations.literal: In the third year of Zhiyuan, Shizu ordered his son Huochihardijin to succeed as Idiqut.
translations.idiomatic: In the third Zhiyuan year (1266), the Shizu Emperor appointed his son Huochihardijin Idiqut.

sentences.zh: 海都、帖木叠兒之亂，畏兀兒之民遭亂解散，於是有旨命亦都護收而撫之，其民人在宗王近戚之境者，悉遣還其部，畏兀兒之眾復輯。

translations.literal: In the disorders of Qaidu and Temür-Ochir, the people of the Uyghurs were scattered in chaos; thereupon an edict ordered the Idiqut to gather and console them; those among the people who were in the domains of imperial princes and close kin were all sent back to their tribes, and the multitude of the Uyghurs was again assembled.
translations.idiomatic: During the rebellions of Qaidu and Temür-Ochir, the Uyghur populace was dispersed; an edict then charged the Idiqut to gather and reassure them. Subjects who had strayed into the domains of princes and imperial kin were all returned to their tribes, and the Uyghur people were restored.

sentences.zh: 十二年，都哇、卜思巴等率兵十二萬圍火州，聲言曰：「阿只吉、奧魯只諸王以三十萬之眾，猶不能抗我而自潰，爾敢以孤城當吾鋒乎？」

translations.literal: In the twelfth year, Duwa, Bosipa, and others led an army of one hundred twenty thousand to surround Huozhou, proclaiming: "The princes Achiji and Aoruji with three hundred thousand men still could not withstand us and collapsed—will you dare hold a lone city against our edge?"
translations.idiomatic: In the twelfth year Duwa, Bosipa, and others invested Huozhou with one hundred twenty thousand men, declaring, "Princes Achiji and Aoruji with three hundred thousand troops could not stand against us and fled—will you hold a solitary city against our blades?"

sentences.zh: 亦都護曰：「吾聞忠臣不事二主，吾生以此城為家，死以此城為墓，終不能從爾也。」

translations.literal: The Idiqut said: "I have heard that a loyal minister does not serve two masters; I was born with this city as my home and will die with this city as my tomb—I absolutely cannot follow you."
translations.idiomatic: The Idiqut replied, "A loyal minister serves but one lord. This city is my home in life and my grave in death—I will never yield to you."

sentences.zh: 受圍凡六月，不解。

translations.literal: They were besieged altogether six months without relief.
translations.idiomatic: The siege lasted six full months without breaking.

sentences.zh: 都哇以書系矢射城中曰：「我亦太祖皇帝諸孫，何以不附我？

translations.literal: Duwa attached a letter to an arrow and shot it into the city, saying: "I too am a descendant grandson of Emperor Taizu—why will you not submit to me?
translations.idiomatic: Duwa bound a letter to an arrow and shot it into the city: "I too am a descendant of Taizu—why do you refuse to join me?

sentences.zh: 且爾祖嘗尚公主矣。

translations.literal: Moreover, your ancestor once married an imperial princess.
translations.idiomatic: Your forebear once married an imperial princess.

sentences.zh: 爾能以女與我，我則休兵，不然則急攻爾。」

translations.literal: If you can give me your daughter, I will cease troops; otherwise I will press the attack upon you."
translations.idiomatic: Give me your daughter and I will lift the siege; otherwise I shall storm you without mercy."

sentences.zh: 其民相與言曰：「城中食且盡，力已困，都哇攻不止，則相與俱亡矣。」

translations.literal: The people together said: "Food in the city is nearly exhausted, strength is already strained, and if Duwa's attack does not cease, we will all perish together."
translations.idiomatic: The townsfolk said among themselves, "Our stores are nearly gone, our strength spent; if Duwa does not relent, we shall all die together."

sentences.zh: 亦都護曰：「吾豈惜一女而不以救民命乎！

translations.literal: The Idiqut said: "How could I cherish one daughter and not use her to save the people's lives!
translations.idiomatic: The Idiqut said, "Would I cling to one daughter rather than save my people's lives?

sentences.zh: 然吾終不能與之相見。」

translations.literal: Yet I absolutely cannot meet him face to face."
translations.idiomatic: Yet I could never bring myself to meet him in person."

sentences.zh: 以其女也立亦黑迷失別吉厚載以茵，引繩縋城下而與之，都哇解去。

translations.literal: He sent his daughter Yilian Yiqimishi Beygi heavily cushioned on a litter, lowered her by rope from the city wall and gave her to them; Duwa withdrew.
translations.idiomatic: He sent his daughter Yilian Yiqimishi Beygi down from the walls on thick cushions in a litter lowered by rope; Duwa then withdrew.

sentences.zh: 其後入朝，帝嘉其功，錫以重賞，妻以公主曰巴巴哈兒，定宗之女也。

translations.literal: Afterwards when he came to court, the Emperor praised his achievement, bestowed heavy rewards, and gave him in marriage the Princess Baba Har, daughter of Dingzong.
translations.idiomatic: When he later attended court, the Emperor commended his service, granted lavish rewards, and married him to Princess Baba Har, daughter of Dingzong.

sentences.zh: 又賜鈔十萬錠以賑其民。

translations.literal: He also bestowed one hundred thousand ingots of paper money to relieve his people.
translations.idiomatic: He also gave one hundred thousand ingots of paper currency to succor his people.

sentences.zh: 還鎮火州，屯於州南哈密力之地，兵力尚寡，北方軍忽至其地，大戰力盡，遂死之。

translations.literal: Returning to guard Huozhou, he encamped south of the prefecture at Hamili; military strength was still scant when northern troops suddenly arrived; they fought a great battle until strength was exhausted and he died in it.
translations.idiomatic: Returning to garrison Huozhou, he encamped south of the city at Hamili. His forces were still weak when northern troops suddenly appeared; he fought until utterly spent and died on the field.

sentences.zh: 帖木兒補化，大德中，尚公主曰朵兒只思蠻，闊端太子孫女也。

translations.literal: Temur Buqa—in the Dade era married the Princess Duo'erzhisiman, granddaughter of Prince Kötö.
translations.idiomatic: Temur Buqa: during the Dade reign he married Princess Duo'erzhisiman, a granddaughter of Prince Kötö.

sentences.zh: 至大中，從父入覲，備宿衛。

translations.literal: In the Zhida era he followed his father to attend court and served in the palace guard.
translations.idiomatic: In the Zhida period he accompanied his father to court and joined the imperial guard.

sentences.zh: 又事皇太后於東朝，拜中奉大夫，領大都護事。

translations.literal: He again served the Empress Dowager in the Eastern Palace, was appointed Grand Master for Thorough Counsel and overseer of the Office of the Metropolitan Protectorate.
translations.idiomatic: He also attended the Empress Dowager in the Eastern Palace, receiving appointment as Grand Master for Thorough Counsel in charge of the Metropolitan Protectorate.

sentences.zh: 又以資善大夫出為鞏昌等處都總帥達魯花赤。

translations.literal: Again with the title of Grand Master for Being Worthy he went out as darughachi general commander of Ganchang and other circuits.
translations.idiomatic: He later went out as Grand Master for Being Worthy and darughachi, supreme commander of Ganchang and associated circuits.

sentences.zh: 奔父喪於永昌，請以王爵讓其叔父欽察臺，叔父力辭，乃嗣為亦都護高昌王。

translations.literal: Hurrying to his father's funeral in Yongchang, he requested to yield the princely rank to his uncle Qinjatai; the uncle forcefully declined, and he then succeeded as Idiqut and King of Gaochang.
translations.idiomatic: Rushing to his father's funeral in Yongchang, he asked to yield his princely title to his uncle Qinjatai; when the uncle firmly refused, he succeeded as Idiqut and King of Gaochang.

sentences.zh: 至治中，領甘肅諸軍，仍治其部。

translations.literal: In the Zhizhi era he commanded Gansu forces and still governed his tribe.
translations.idiomatic: Under Zhizhi he commanded Gansu troops while still governing his people.

sentences.zh: 泰定中召還，與威順王寬徹不花、宣靖王買奴、靖安王闊不花分鎮襄陽。

translations.literal: In the Taiding era he was summoned back to share defense of Xiangyang with Princes Weishun Kuanchibuhua, Xuanjing Mainu, and Jing'an Kuobuhua.
translations.idiomatic: In the Taiding era he was recalled to garrison Xiangyang jointly with Princes Weishun Kuanchibuhua, Xuanjing Mainu, and Jing'an Kuobuhua.

sentences.zh: 俄拜開府儀同三司、湖廣行省平章政事。

translations.literal: Soon he was appointed Pillar of the State, ceremonial equal to the Three Excellencies, and Pingzhang of the Huguang Branch Secretariat.
translations.idiomatic: Shortly afterward he was made Pillar of the State with ceremonial rank equal to the Three Excellencies and Pingzhang of the Huguang Branch Secretariat.

sentences.zh: 文宗召至京師，佐平大難。

translations.literal: Wenzong summoned him to the capital to assist in settling the great crisis.
translations.idiomatic: Emperor Wenzong summoned him to the capital to help quell the great upheaval.

sentences.zh: 時湖廣左丞有以忌嫉害政者，詔命誅之。

translations.literal: At that time a left assistant minister of Huguang, out of envy and jealousy, was harming government; an edict ordered his execution.
translations.idiomatic: A left assistant minister in Huguang was undermining administration out of jealousy; an edict ordered his death.

sentences.zh: 帖木兒補化乃為申請曰：「是誠有罪，然不至死。」

translations.literal: Temur Buqa then appealed saying: "This man is indeed guilty, yet not to the point of death."
translations.idiomatic: Temur Buqa pleaded, "He is guilty, but not deserving of death."

sentences.zh: 人服其雅量。

translations.literal: People admired his generous measure.
translations.idiomatic: People admired his magnanimity.

sentences.zh: 天歷元年，拜開府儀同三司、上柱國、錄軍國重事、知樞密院事。

translations.literal: In the first year of Tianli he was appointed Pillar of the State, Upper Pillar of the State, Recorder of Weighty Affairs in Military and State Affairs, and controller of the Bureau of Military Affairs.
translations.idiomatic: In Tianli year one (1328) he became Pillar of the State, Upper Pillar of the State, Recorder of Weighty Military and State Affairs, and controller of the Bureau of Military Affairs.

sentences.zh: 明年正月，以舊官勛封拜中書左丞相。

translations.literal: In the first month of the next year, with former office and meritorious enfeoffment he was appointed left chancellor of the Central Secretariat.
translations.idiomatic: The following first month he was appointed Left Chancellor of the Central Secretariat, retaining his former honors.

sentences.zh: 三月，加太子詹事；

translations.literal: In the third month, he was additionally made Supervisor of the Heir Apparent's Household;
translations.idiomatic: In the third month he was additionally made Supervisor of the Heir Apparent's Household;

sentences.zh: 十月，拜御史大夫。

translations.literal: In the tenth month, he was appointed Censor-in-Chief.
translations.idiomatic: In the tenth month he was made Censor-in-Chief.

sentences.zh: 其弟篯吉乃以讓嗣為亦都護高昌王。

translations.literal: His younger brother Jijinai yielded the succession and became Idiqut and King of Gaochang.
translations.idiomatic: His younger brother Jijinai received the succession as Idiqut and King of Gaochang.

sentences.zh: ○鐵邁赤虎都鐵木祿 ○塔海

translations.literal: ○ Tie Maichi: Hudutieimu Lu ○ Tahai
translations.idiomatic: ○ Tie Maichi: Hudutieimu Lu ○ Tahai

sentences.zh: 虎都鐵木祿好讀書，與學士大夫遊，字之曰漢卿。

translations.literal: Hudutieimu Lu loved reading books and associated with scholar-officials; his courtesy name was Hanqing.
translations.idiomatic: Hudutieimu Lu loved books and kept company with scholar-officials, who styled him Hanqing ("Han minister").

sentences.zh: 仁宗嘗顧左右曰：「虎都鐵木祿字漢卿，漢名卿不讓也，汝等以漢卿名之宜矣。」

translations.literal: Renzong once looked about him and said: "Hudutieimu Lu's courtesy name Hanqing—among Han names 'Qing' is not to be yielded; you all should suitably call him Hanqing."
translations.idiomatic: Renzong once remarked to those around him, "Hudutieimu Lu bears the courtesy name Hanqing—among Han names 'Qing' is no small honor; you should all address him as Hanqing."

sentences.zh: 其母姓劉氏，故人又稱之曰劉漢卿雲。

translations.literal: His mother's surname was Liu; therefore people also called him Liu Hanqing.
translations.idiomatic: His mother was surnamed Liu, so people also called him Liu Hanqing.

sentences.zh: 至元十一年，從丞相伯顏渡江。

translations.literal: In the eleventh year of Zhiyuan he followed Chancellor Bayan in crossing the Yangzi.
translations.idiomatic: In Zhiyuan year eleven (1274) he crossed the Yangzi with Chancellor Bayan.

sentences.zh: 既取宋，遣視宋故宮室，護帑藏。

translations.literal: After the Song was taken, he was sent to inspect the former Song palace dwellings and protect the treasuries and stores.
translations.idiomatic: After the Song fell, he was sent to inspect the former Song palaces and safeguard the treasuries.

sentences.zh: 諭下明、越等州。

translations.literal: He issued proclamations down to Ming, Yue, and other prefectures.
translations.idiomatic: He issued instructions throughout Ming, Yue, and neighboring prefectures.

sentences.zh: 從平章奧魯入覲，授忠顯校慰總把，再轉昭信校尉。

translations.literal: Following Pingzhang Orlu to attend court, he was appointed Chief Commandant of Loyal Manifestation and then transferred to Commandant of Manifest Integrity.
translations.idiomatic: Following Pingzhang Orlu to court, he was appointed Chief Commandant of Loyal Manifestation, then promoted to Commandant of Manifest Integrity.

sentences.zh: 二十二年，授奉訓大夫，荊湖占城等處行中書省理問官。

translations.literal: In the twenty-second year he was appointed Grand Master for Training and investigating magistrate of the Jinghu-Zhancheng Branch Secretariat and other places.
translations.idiomatic: In the twenty-second year he became Grand Master for Training and investigating magistrate of the Jinghu-Zhancheng circuit.

sentences.zh: 時行省之名曰荊湖占城，曰荊湖，曰湖廣，凡三改。

translations.literal: At that time the name of the branch secretariat was called Jinghu-Zhancheng, called Jinghu, called Huguang—in all three changes.
translations.idiomatic: The branch secretariat changed its name three times: Jinghu-Zhancheng, then Jinghu, then Huguang.

sentences.zh: 理問一日以軍事入奏，敷陳辨白有指趣，世祖大悅，若曰：「辭簡意明，令人樂於聽受，昔以其兄阿裏警敏捷給，令侍左右，斯人顧不勝耶？」

translations.literal: One day the investigating magistrate entered court on military affairs and set forth his memorial with pointed clarity; Shizu was greatly pleased and as if to say: "The words are concise and the meaning clear, making one delight to listen—formerly his elder brother Ali was alert and nimble in service, ordered to attend at the side; is this man not still more capable?"
translations.idiomatic: One day, reporting on military affairs, he presented his memorial with crisp, purposeful argument. The Shizu Emperor was delighted and remarked, "Concise words and clear sense—pleasant to hear. His elder brother Ali was quick and resourceful beside me; can this one not do even better?"

sentences.zh: 敕都護脫因納誌之。

translations.literal: An edict ordered the Metropolitan Protector Tuoyinnah to record this.
translations.idiomatic: He ordered Metropolitan Protector Tuoyinnah to note this.

sentences.zh: 平章政事程鵬飛建議征日本，奏漢卿為征東省郎中。

translations.literal: Pingzhang Cheng Pengfei proposed campaigning against Japan and memorialized Hanqing as bureau director of the Eastern Campaign Secretariat.
translations.idiomatic: Pingzhang Cheng Pengfei proposed an expedition against Japan and recommended Hanqing as bureau director of the Eastern Campaign Directorate.

sentences.zh: 帝顧脫因納，若曰：「鵬飛南士也，猶知其能。

translations.literal: The Emperor looked at Tuoyinnah as if to say: "Pengfei is a southern man, yet still knows his ability.
translations.idiomatic: The Emperor glanced at Tuoyinnah as if to say, "Even Pengfei, a southerner, recognizes his talent.

sentences.zh: 姑聽之，候還，朕自錄任。」

translations.literal: For the moment let him go; when he returns I myself will record and appoint him."
translations.idiomatic: Let him go for now; when he returns I shall appoint him myself."

sentences.zh: 征東省罷，征漢卿還。

translations.literal: When the Eastern Campaign Secretariat was abolished, Hanqing was summoned back.
translations.idiomatic: When the Eastern Campaign Directorate was dissolved, Hanqing was recalled.

sentences.zh: 丞相阿裏海牙以湖廣行省機密事重，舍漢卿無可用者，遣郎中嶽洛也奴奏留，從之。

translations.literal: Chancellor Alihaiya, because Huguang Branch Secretariat confidential affairs were weighty and aside from Hanqing there was no one usable, sent bureau director Yueluoyenu to memorialize to retain him, and it was approved.
translations.idiomatic: Chancellor Alihaiya, finding Huguang's confidential affairs too weighty to entrust to anyone but Hanqing, had bureau director Yueluoyenu petition to retain him, and the request was granted.

sentences.zh: 二十一年，從皇子鎮南王征交趾。

translations.literal: In the twenty-first year he followed Prince Zhennan in campaigning against Annam.
translations.idiomatic: In the twenty-first year he followed Prince Zhennan on the Annam campaign.

sentences.zh: 比還鄂時，權臣方擅威福，遂退處於家。

translations.literal: When he returned to Ezhou, powerful ministers were monopolizing authority and fortune; he thereupon withdrew and dwelt at home.
translations.idiomatic: On his return to Ezhou, powerful ministers were monopolizing power; he withdrew to live at home.

sentences.zh: 二十八年，詔太傅、右丞相順德王答剌罕擒權奸於鄂。

translations.literal: In the twenty-eighth year an edict ordered Grand Tutor and Right Chancellor the Prince of Shunde, Daruqan, to arrest the powerful traitors at E.
translations.idiomatic: In the twenty-eighth year an edict ordered Grand Tutor and Right Chancellor, Prince of Shunde Daruqan, to seize the powerful traitors at Ezhou.

sentences.zh: 答剌罕遂拜湖廣行中書省平章政事，詢舊人知方面之務者，眾薦漢卿，遣使即南陽家居驛致武昌，奏事京師，帝嘉之，擢給事中。

translations.literal: Daruqan thereupon was appointed Pingzhang of the Huguang Branch Secretariat; inquiring of old retainers who knew frontier affairs, the multitude recommended Hanqing; he sent envoys from the postal station at his Nanyang home to fetch him to Wuchang; he memorialized affairs at the capital; the Emperor praised this and promoted him to Supervising Censor.
translations.idiomatic: Daruqan was then made Pingzhang of Huguang. Seeking veterans who knew regional affairs, many recommended Hanqing; envoys were sent from the post relay at his Nanyang home to bring him to Wuchang. His memorials reached the capital; the Emperor commended him and promoted him to Supervising Censor.

sentences.zh: 居再歲，提刑按察司改肅政廉訪司，臺臣奏授奉議大夫、廣西海北道副使，陛辭，留之仍舊職。

translations.literal: After two years in office, the Punishment Investigation and Surveillance Office was changed to the Office for Upholding Justice and Incorrupt Government; censorate officials memorialized appointing him Grand Master for Discussion, deputy commissioner of the Guangxi Haibei Circuit; at audience he was retained in his former post.
translations.idiomatic: After two years the Punishment Investigation Office became the Office for Upholding Justice and Incorrupt Government. Censors recommended him as Grand Master for Discussion, deputy commissioner of Guangxi Haibei Circuit, but at his farewell audience he was kept in his former post.

sentences.zh: 既而湖廣行省平章政事劉國傑奏伐交趾，造戰船五百於廣東，帝曰：「此重事也，須才幹臣乃濟用。」

translations.literal: Afterwards Huguang Pingzhang Liu Guojie memorialized campaigning against Annam and building five hundred war vessels in Guangdong; the Emperor said: "This is a weighty affair and requires a talented capable minister to accomplish it."
translations.idiomatic: Later Huguang Pingzhang Liu Guojie proposed an Annam expedition and building five hundred warships in Guangdong. The Emperor said, "This is a weighty matter—it needs a capable minister."

sentences.zh: 以漢卿督匠南方，敕曰：「汝還，當顯汝於眾。」

translations.literal: He appointed Hanqing to supervise craftsmen in the south; the edict said: "When you return, I shall make you manifest among the multitude."
translations.idiomatic: Hanqing was appointed to supervise southern shipwrights, with an edict saying, "When you return, I shall display your merit before all."

sentences.zh: 因頓首謝。

translations.literal: He thereupon bowed his head in thanks.
translations.idiomatic: He bowed deeply in thanks.

sentences.zh: 事既集，帝崩，遷福建行省郎中，朝列大夫、漢陽監府，中順大夫、湖南宣慰副使。

translations.literal: When the affair was concluded the Emperor died; he was transferred to bureau director of the Fujian Branch Secretariat, Court Dignitary of the Second Grade, Overseer of the Hanyang Directorate, Grand Master of the Third Grade, and deputy commissioner of the Hunan Pacification Commission.
translations.idiomatic: When the work was finished the Emperor died. He was transferred to bureau director of Fujian, Court Dignitary of the Second Grade and overseer of the Hanyang directorate, then Grand Master of the Third Grade and deputy pacification commissioner of Hunan.

sentences.zh: 峒酋岑雄叛，奉詔開諭，頑獷帖服。

translations.literal: The tribal chief of the Dong, Qin Xiong, rebelled; he received an edict to open persuasion, and the stubborn and violent submitted.
translations.idiomatic: Dong chieftain Qin Xiong rebelled; commissioned to persuade him, Hanqing brought the recalcitrant to submission.

sentences.zh: 改太中大夫、河南行中書省郎中，通議大夫、同僉樞密院事，拜禮部尚書。

translations.literal: He was changed to Grand Master of the Second Grade, bureau director of the Henan Branch Secretariat, Grand Master for Governance, vice controller of the Bureau of Military Affairs, and appointed Minister of Rites.
translations.idiomatic: He rose to Grand Master of the Second Grade and bureau director of Henan, then Grand Master for Governance and vice controller of Military Affairs, and was appointed Minister of Rites.

sentences.zh: 大臣奏核實江南民田，漢卿奉詔使江西，以田額舊定，重擾民不便，置不問。

translations.literal: Great ministers memorialized verifying Jiangnan civilian fields; Hanqing received the edict to mission to Jiangxi; because the field quotas were long fixed and re-survey would heavily disturb the people and be inconvenient, he set it aside without inquiry.
translations.idiomatic: Ministers proposed verifying Jiangnan land holdings; Hanqing was sent to Jiangxi. Finding the quotas long fixed and a new survey would only harass the people, he left the matter untouched.

sentences.zh: 止奏茶、漕置局十有七所，以七品印章敕授局官五十一員，增中統課緡五十萬。

translations.literal: He only memorialized establishing seventeen offices for tea and transport; with seventh-rank seals an edict appointed fifty-one office officials, increasing Zhongtong tax paper currency by five hundred thousand.
translations.idiomatic: He memorialized only the establishment of seventeen tea and grain transport offices, with edicts appointing fifty-one officials bearing seventh-rank seals and increasing Zhongtong paper tax currency by five hundred thousand.

sentences.zh: 轉正議大夫、兵部尚書。

translations.literal: He was transferred to Grand Master for Governance, Minister of War.
translations.idiomatic: He was transferred to Grand Master for Governance and Minister of War.

sentences.zh: 未幾命為中奉大夫、荊湖北道宣慰使，已命，復留之。

translations.literal: Before long he was ordered Grand Master for Thorough Counsel, Pacification Commissioner of the Jinghu North Circuit; already ordered, he was again retained.
translations.idiomatic: Soon he was appointed Grand Master for Thorough Counsel and Pacification Commissioner of Jinghu North Circuit, but after the order was issued he was kept at court once more.

sentences.zh: 延祐三年，大臣以浙東倭奴商舶貿易致亂，奏遣漢卿宣慰閩、浙，撫戢兵民，海陸為之靜謐云。

translations.literal: In the third year of Yanyou, great ministers because eastern Zhejiang Japanese pirate merchant ships' trade caused disorder memorialized dispatching Hanqing to pacify and comfort Fujian and Zhejiang, soothing troops and people; by land and sea thereby became quiet and tranquil.
translations.idiomatic: In the third year of Yanyou (1316), ministers reported that trade by Japanese pirate merchants in eastern Zhejiang had sparked unrest. They memorialized sending Hanqing as pacification commissioner to Fujian and Zhejiang to soothe soldiers and civilians, and peace returned on land and sea.

sentences.zh: 從子塔海。

translations.literal: [His] nephew Tahai.
translations.idiomatic: His nephew Tahai.

sentences.zh: 塔海，漢卿兄子也。

translations.literal: Tahai was Hanqing's elder brother's son.
translations.idiomatic: Tahai was the son of Hanqing's elder brother.

sentences.zh: 世祖時，從土土哈充哈剌赤。

translations.literal: In Shizu's time, he followed Tutuha to serve as qaračin.
translations.idiomatic: Under Khubilai he followed Tutuha and served in the qaračin, the imperial guard corps.

sentences.zh: 至元二十四年，扈駕征乃顏。

translations.literal: In the twenty-fourth year of Zhiyuan, he escorted the imperial procession to campaign against Nayan.
translations.idiomatic: In Zhiyuan 24 (1287) he accompanied the Emperor on the campaign against Nayan.

sentences.zh: 二十六年，入覲，帝命充寶兒赤，扈駕至和林，賜只孫冠服。

translations.literal: In the twenty-sixth year he entered audience; the Emperor ordered him to serve as ba'erchi, escorting the procession to Karakorum, and bestowed jisun court robes.
translations.idiomatic: In the twenty-sixth year he came to court; the Emperor appointed him ba'erchi and he escorted the imperial retinue to Karakorum, receiving jisun ceremonial dress as a gift.

sentences.zh: 大德四年，授中書直省舍人。

translations.literal: In the fourth year of Dade, he was appointed Secretariat Attendant of the Direct Secretariat.
translations.idiomatic: In Dade 4 (1300) he was appointed an attendant of the Central Secretariat's direct office.

sentences.zh: 遷中書客省副使。

translations.literal: He was transferred to deputy commissioner of the Secretariat Guest Office.
translations.idiomatic: He was promoted to deputy commissioner of the Secretariat Guest Office.

sentences.zh: 武宗即位，賜中統鈔五百錠，以旌其能。

translations.literal: When Wuzong acceded, he was granted five hundred ding of Zhongtong paper currency, to commend his ability.
translations.idiomatic: When Wuzong took the throne, Tahai received five hundred ding of Zhongtong paper notes in recognition of his merit.

sentences.zh: 尋進和林行省理問所官，改通政僉院。

translations.literal: Soon he advanced to official of the Karakorum Branch Secretariat investigating magistrate office; he was changed to vice commissioner of the Transmission Bureau.
translations.idiomatic: He was soon promoted to an investigating magistrate of the Karakorum branch secretariat, then transferred to vice commissioner of the Transmission Bureau.

sentences.zh: 歷和寧路總管，改汴梁。

translations.literal: He served successively as route commander of Henning Route; then was transferred to Bianliang.
translations.idiomatic: He served as route commander of Henning and later of Bianliang.

sentences.zh: 先是，朝廷令民自實田土，有司繩以峻法，民多虛報以塞命，其後差稅無所於征，民多逃竄流移者。

translations.literal: Previously, the court ordered people to self-register their fields; the officials bound them with severe law; the people mostly made false reports to fulfill the order; afterward land tax had nowhere from which to be levied; many people fled and wandered away.
translations.idiomatic: Earlier the court had ordered households to declare their land holdings themselves. Local officials enforced the policy harshly, and many people filed inflated returns merely to satisfy the order. Later there was no solid basis for levying taxes, and large numbers fled or drifted away.

sentences.zh: 塔海以其弊言於朝。

translations.literal: Tahai spoke of this abuse to the court.
translations.idiomatic: Tahai reported this abuse to the court.

sentences.zh: 由是省民間虛糧二十二萬，民賴以安。

translations.literal: From this were reduced two hundred twenty thousand [units of] false grain levies among the people; the people relied on this to be at peace.
translations.idiomatic: As a result, two hundred twenty thousand units of inflated grain tax were struck from the rolls, and the people were relieved.

sentences.zh: 後改任廬州，時有飛蝗北來，民患之，塔海禱於天，蝗乃引去，亦有墮水死者，人皆以為異。

translations.literal: Later he was transferred to Luzhou; at the time flying locusts came from the north; the people suffered from them; Tahai prayed to Heaven; the locusts then withdrew; some also fell into water and died; people all regarded it as extraordinary.
translations.idiomatic: Later, posted to Luzhou, he faced a plague of locusts sweeping in from the north. Tahai prayed for deliverance, and the swarm withdrew; some drowned as well. People took it for a marvel.

sentences.zh: 民乏食，開廩減直，俾民糴之，所活甚眾。

translations.literal: When the people lacked food, he opened the granaries and lowered prices, causing the people to buy grain; those saved were very many.
translations.idiomatic: When famine struck, he opened the granaries and sold grain at reduced prices, saving a great many lives.

sentences.zh: 天歷元年冬十月，樞密院臣奏以塔海充樞密僉院，守潼關及河中府。

translations.literal: In the tenth month of winter in the first year of Tianli, Bureau of Military Affairs officials memorialized appointing Tahai vice controller of Military Affairs, guarding Tong Pass and Hezhong Prefecture.
translations.idiomatic: In the tenth month of winter, Tianli 1 (1328), the Privy Council recommended Tahai as vice controller of Military Affairs to hold Tong Pass and Hezhong Prefecture.

sentences.zh: 帝遣人馳賜白金鈔幣，宣授僉書樞密院事。

translations.literal: The Emperor sent a person post-haste to bestow white gold and paper currency; he was proclaimed and appointed vice secretary of the Bureau of Military Affairs.
translations.idiomatic: The Emperor sent couriers bearing white silver and paper currency and formally appointed him vice secretary of the Privy Council.

sentences.zh: 未幾西軍犯南陽，督諸衛兵往平之。

translations.literal: Before long the Western Army invaded Nanyang; he supervised the various guard troops to go pacify them.
translations.idiomatic: Soon afterward rebel western troops invaded Nanyang, and he led the guard units to suppress them.

sentences.zh: 至其地，首率勇士與帖木哥等戰，摧其前鋒將，奪其旗鼓，西軍敗走。

translations.literal: Arriving at that place, he first led brave warriors to battle Temüge and others; he shattered their vanguard general; seized their banners and drums; the Western Army was defeated and fled.
translations.idiomatic: On reaching the scene he led the charge against Temüge and his fellows, breaking their vanguard commander and seizing their standards and drums. The western forces broke and fled.

sentences.zh: 賜三珠虎符，進大都督，累官資善大夫。

translations.literal: He was granted a three-pearl tiger tally; promoted to Grand Commander; accumulated office to Grand Master for Good Counsel.
translations.idiomatic: He was awarded a three-pearl tiger tally, promoted to Grand Commander, and eventually rose to Grand Master for Good Counsel.

sentences.zh: ○按紥兒

translations.literal: ○ Anzha'er
translations.idiomatic: ○ Anzha'er

sentences.zh: 按紥兒，拓跋氏，嘗扈從太祖南征。

translations.literal: Anzha'er, of the Tuoba clan, once escorted and followed Taizu on the southern campaign.
translations.idiomatic: Anzha'er, of the Tuoba clan, once accompanied Genghis Khan on the southern campaign.

sentences.zh: 歲丙子，復從定諸部有功，命領蒙古軍為前鋒，時木華黎暨博爾術為左右萬戶長，各以其屬為翊衛。

translations.literal: In the year bingzi, he again followed in pacifying the various tribes with merit; he was ordered to lead Mongol troops as vanguard; at that time Muqali together with Borokhula were left and right myriarch commanders, each using their followers as flank guards.
translations.idiomatic: In the bingzi year (1216) he again distinguished himself in subduing the tribes and was ordered to lead the Mongol vanguard. Muqali and Borokhula served as the left and right myriarchs, each commanding his own men as escort forces.

sentences.zh: 太祖命木華黎為太師國王都行省承制行事，兵臨燕、遼、營、青、齊、魯、趙、韓、魏，皆下。

translations.literal: Taizu ordered Muqali as Grand Preceptor, King, Branch Secretariat acting by imperial commission; troops pressed upon Yan, Liao, Ying, Qing, Qi, Lu, Zhao, Han, Wei—all fell.
translations.idiomatic: Genghis Khan appointed Muqali Grand Preceptor and King, with authority to govern through a branch secretariat on campaign. His armies overran Yan, Liao, Ying, Qing, Qi, Lu, Zhao, Han, and Wei.

sentences.zh: 歲己卯，河中府降，兵北還，以按紥兒領前鋒總帥，仍統所部兵屯平陽以備金，攝國王事。

translations.literal: In the year jimao, Hezhong Prefecture surrendered; the army returned north; Anzha'er was made vanguard commander-in-chief, still commanding his own troops stationed at Pingyang to guard against Jin, acting in the King's affairs.
translations.idiomatic: In jimao (1219) Hezhong Prefecture submitted and the army withdrew north. Anzha'er was left as vanguard commander-in-chief, holding Pingyang with his troops to watch the Jin border and acting in Muqali's stead.

sentences.zh: 時金將乞石烈氏擁兵數為邊患，然畏按紥兒威名，不敢輕犯其境。

translations.literal: At that time Jin general Qishilie clan held troops and several times was a border menace; yet he feared Anzha'er's formidable reputation and did not dare lightly violate his territory.
translations.idiomatic: The Jin general Qishilie repeatedly raided the frontier with a large force, but he feared Anzha'er's reputation and dared not lightly cross into his territory.

sentences.zh: 歲壬午，元帥石天應守河中府，屯中條山，金侯將軍率昆弟兵十餘萬夜襲河中，天應遣偏裨吳權府率五百兵出東門，伏兩谷間。

translations.literal: In the year renwu, Marshal Shi Tianying guarded Hezhong Prefecture, encamped on Zhongtiao Mountain; Jin General Hou led brothers' troops more than one hundred thousand in a night assault on Hezhong; Tianying sent lieutenant Wu Quanfu leading five hundred troops out the east gate, ambushing between two ravines.
translations.idiomatic: In renwu (1222) Marshal Shi Tianying held Hezhong Prefecture from a camp on Zhongtiao Mountain. The Jin commander General Hou led more than one hundred thousand men—including his brothers' forces—in a night attack. Tianying sent Lieutenant Wu Quanfu with five hundred men out the east gate to lie in wait between two valleys.

sentences.zh: 諭之曰：「俟其半過，即翼擊之，俾腹背受敵，即成禽矣。」

translations.literal: He instructed him saying: "Wait until half have passed, then flank and strike them, causing them to suffer enemy front and back—they will then be captured."
translations.idiomatic: He instructed him: "When half their force has passed, strike from the flank so they are caught between our blades and captured whole."

sentences.zh: 吳醉，敵至，聲援弗繼，城遂陷，天應死焉，遂燔其城，屠其民。

translations.literal: Wu was drunk; the enemy arrived; supporting attacks did not follow; the city then fell; Tianying died thereupon; they then burned the city and slaughtered the people.
translations.idiomatic: Wu was drunk. When the enemy arrived, reinforcements never came. The city fell, Tianying was killed, and the Jin forces burned it and massacred the inhabitants.

sentences.zh: 將趨中條，按紥兒進兵擊之，斬首數萬級，逃免者僅十數。

translations.literal: About to advance toward Zhongtiao, Anzha'er advanced troops to strike them; heads cut numbered tens of thousands; those who escaped were only a dozen-odd.
translations.idiomatic: As they marched toward Zhongtiao, Anzha'er gave chase and killed tens of thousands; only a dozen or so escaped.

sentences.zh: 歲癸未春，至聞喜縣西下馬村，木華黎卒，詔以子孛魯襲其爵，時平陽重地，令按紥兒居守。

translations.literal: In spring of the year guiwei, arriving at Xiamacun west of Wenxi County, Muqali died; an edict ordered his son Bolu to inherit his rank; at that time Pingyang was an important place; Anzha'er was ordered to remain and guard.
translations.idiomatic: In the spring of guiwei (1223), near Xiamacun west of Wenxi County, Muqali died. An edict had his son Bolu succeed to his title. Pingyang being strategically vital, Anzha'er was ordered to hold it.

sentences.zh: 歲庚寅，孛魯由雲中圍衛州，金將武仙恐，退保潞東十餘里原上，孛魯馳至沁南，未立鼓，乞石烈引兵襲其後，孛魯戰失利，輜重人口皆陷沒，按紥兒妻奴丹氏亦被獲，拘於大梁。

translations.literal: In the year gengyin, Bolu from Yunzhong besieged Weizhou; Jin general Wu Xian feared; retreated to guard on the plain more than ten li east of Lu; Bolu galloped to the south of Qin; before drums were set, Qishilie led troops to raid his rear; Bolu battled with defeat; baggage train and people all were lost; Anzha'er's wife Lady Nudan was also captured; detained at Daliang.
translations.idiomatic: In gengyin (1230) Bolu marched from Yunzhong to besiege Weizhou. The Jin general Wu Xian withdrew in alarm to a plain east of Lu. Bolu raced south of the Qin River, but before his camp was fully set Qishilie struck from the rear. Bolu was defeated; baggage and dependents were lost, and Anzha'er's wife Lady Nudan was taken captive to Daliang (Kaifeng).

sentences.zh: 金主聞按紥兒威名，召奴丹氏見，奴丹氏色莊言正，不為動。

translations.literal: The Jin ruler heard Anzha'er's formidable reputation; summoned Lady Nudan to audience; Lady Nudan's expression was stern and speech upright; she was not moved.
translations.idiomatic: Hearing of Anzha'er's fame, the Jin emperor summoned Lady Nudan. She appeared with stern bearing and upright words, unmoved.

sentences.zh: 金主因謂之曰：「今縱爾還，能偕爾夫來，當厚賞爾。」

translations.literal: The Jin ruler thereupon said to her: "Now if I release you to return, if you can bring your husband together, I shall richly reward you."
translations.idiomatic: The Jin emperor said to her, "If I release you now and you bring your husband with you, I shall richly reward you."

sentences.zh: 奴丹氏佯諾之，遂得還。

translations.literal: Lady Nudan feigned assent; then was able to return.
translations.idiomatic: Lady Nudan feigned agreement and was allowed to go home.

sentences.zh: 太宗聞而義之，召見，褒賚甚厚，遂詔預其夫前鋒事。

translations.literal: Taizong heard and approved her righteousness; summoned her to audience; praised and rewarded very generously; then decreed her to participate in her husband's vanguard affairs.
translations.idiomatic: Ögedei heard and admired her conduct. He summoned her, lavished praise and gifts, and decreed that she might share in her husband's vanguard command.

sentences.zh: 帝率從弟按只吉歹、口溫不花大王、皇弟四太子暨國王孛魯征潞州、鳳翔。

translations.literal: The Emperor led junior cousin Ajirighaday, Prince Kökeönggü, the Emperor's younger brother the Fourth Prince, together with King Bolu to campaign against Luzhou and Fengxiang.
translations.idiomatic: The Emperor led his cousin Ajirighaday, Prince Kökeönggü, his younger brother the Fourth Prince, and King Bolu against Luzhou and Fengxiang.

sentences.zh: 至鈞州三峰山，金將完顏合達引兵十五萬來戰，俘其同僉移剌不花等，悉誅之。

translations.literal: Arriving at Sanfeng Mountain in Junzhou, Jin general Wanyan Hedai led one hundred fifty thousand troops to battle; captured his vice commissioner Yelü Buhua and others; all were executed.
translations.idiomatic: At Sanfeng Mountain near Junzhou, the Jin commander Wanyan Hedai came with one hundred fifty thousand men. They captured his vice commissioner Yelü Buhua and others and put them all to death.

sentences.zh: 明年壬辰春，三月，帝班師北還，命偕都元帥唆伯臺圍汴。

translations.literal: The next year, spring of renchen, third month, the Emperor withdrew the army north; ordered together with Grand Commander Suobatai to besiege Bian.
translations.idiomatic: The following spring, in the third month of renchen (1232), the Emperor marched north and ordered Suobatai to join in besieging Bian (Kaifeng).

sentences.zh: 城中識按紥兒旗幟，懼曰：「其妻猶勇且義，況其夫乎！」

translations.literal: In the city they recognized Anzha'er's banner flags; feared and said: "His wife is still brave and righteous—how much more so his husband!"
translations.idiomatic: Seeing Anzha'er's banners, the city folk said in dread, "If his wife is so brave and upright, how much more fearsome must he be!"

sentences.zh: 歲甲午，金亡，詔封功臣，賜平陽戶六百一十有四、驅戶三十、獵戶四。

translations.literal: In the year jiawu, Jin perished; an edict enfeoffed meritorious ministers; granted Pingyang households six hundred fourteen, driver households thirty, hunting households four.
translations.idiomatic: In jiawu (1234), with the Jin destroyed, Anzha'er was enfeoffed among the meritorious officials with six hundred fourteen households at Pingyang, thirty driver households, and four hunting households.

sentences.zh: 未幾，以疾卒。

translations.literal: Before long, he died of illness.
translations.idiomatic: Before long he died of illness.

sentences.zh: 子忙漢、拙赤哥。

translations.literal: Sons Manghan and Juochige.
translations.idiomatic: His sons were Manghan and Juochige.

sentences.zh: ○雪不臺

translations.literal: ○ Xuebutai
translations.idiomatic: ○ Xuebutai

sentences.zh: 雪不臺，蒙古部兀良罕氏。

translations.literal: Xuebutai, of the Uyirad clan of the Mongol division.
translations.idiomatic: Xuebutai belonged to the Uyirad clan of the Mongols.

sentences.zh: 遠祖捏裏弼生孛忽都，雄勇有智略。

translations.literal: Remote ancestor Nili'bi bore Börütu; fierce and brave with wisdom and strategy.
translations.idiomatic: His distant forebear Nili'bi fathered Börütu, a man of fierce courage and keen strategy.

sentences.zh: 曾孫合飭溫生哈班、哈不裏。

translations.literal: Great-grandson Hechiwen bore Qaban and Qaburi.
translations.idiomatic: His great-grandson Hechiwen had two sons, Qaban and Qaburi.

sentences.zh: 哈班生二子：長虎魯渾，次雪不臺。

translations.literal: Qaban bore two sons: the elder Qorluqun, the younger Xuebutai.
translations.idiomatic: Qaban's elder son was Qorluqun; the younger was Xuebutai.

sentences.zh: 太祖初建興都於班朱泥河，今龍居河也。

translations.literal: Taizu at first established the capital at Banzhuni River—today Longju River.
translations.idiomatic: Genghis Khan first established his capital on the Banzhuni River—now known as the Longju River.

sentences.zh: 哈班驅群羊入貢，遇盜見執，雪不臺及兄虎魯渾隨至，剌盜殺之，眾潰去，哈班得以羊進帝所，由是父子兄弟以義勇稱。

translations.literal: Qaban drove a flock of sheep to tribute; encountered bandits and was seized; Xuebutai and elder brother Qorluqun followed and arrived; stabbed bandits and killed them; the multitude dispersed and left; Qaban was able to bring the sheep to the Emperor's place; from this father, sons, and brothers were famed for righteousness and courage.
translations.idiomatic: Once when Qaban was driving sheep as tribute, robbers seized him. Xuebutai and Qorluqun came up, killed the robbers, and put them to flight. Qaban delivered the sheep to the Khan, and from that day the family was renowned for steadfast courage.

sentences.zh: 虎魯渾以百夫長西征，破乃蠻，立戰功。

translations.literal: Qorluqun as centurion on the western campaign broke the Naiman and established battle merit.
translations.idiomatic: Qorluqun served as a centurion on the western campaigns, defeated the Naiman, and won distinction in battle.

sentences.zh: 雪不臺以質子襲職，七年，攻桓州，先登，下其城，賜金幣凡一車。

translations.literal: Xuebutai as hostage-son inherited the office; in the seventh year, attacking Huanzhou, he was first to ascend; took its city; granted gold and currency in all one cartload.
translations.idiomatic: Xuebutai succeeded to his post as a hostage-son at court. In the seventh year he led the assault on Huanzhou, was first over the wall, and took the city; he was rewarded with a cartload of gold and cash.

sentences.zh: 十一年，戰滅裏吉眾於蟾河，追其部長玉峪，大破之，遂有其地。

translations.literal: In the eleventh year, battled Möngke's multitude at Chan River; pursued their tribal chief Yuyu; greatly broke them; then possessed that territory.
translations.idiomatic: In the eleventh year he fought Möngke's forces on the Chan River, pursued their chieftain Yuyu, routed them, and seized the territory.

sentences.zh: 扈從征回鶻，其主棄國去，雪不臺率眾追之，回鶻竟走死。

translations.literal: Escorting and following the campaign against the Uyghurs, their lord abandoned the state and fled; Xuebutai led the multitude in pursuit; the Uyghurs ultimately fled to death.
translations.idiomatic: On the campaign against the Uyghurs, when their ruler abandoned his realm, Xuebutai pursued at the head of his men until the Uyghur forces were run down and destroyed.

sentences.zh: 其帑藏之積盡入內府，賜寶珠一銀罌。

translations.literal: Their treasury hoardings all entered the inner treasury; he was granted one silver jar of precious pearls.
translations.idiomatic: The conquered treasury was sent to the imperial storehouse, and he was given a silver jar filled with pearls.

sentences.zh: 十八年，討定欽察，鏖戰斡羅思大小密赤思老，降之，奏滅裏吉、乃蠻、怯烈、杭斤、欽察部千戶，通立一軍。

translations.literal: In the eighteenth year, punished and pacified the Qipchaq; bitterly battled Volosi great and small Michishilao; subdued them; memorialized Möngke, Naiman, Kereyid, Hanggin, Qipchaq tribal centurions, jointly establishing one army.
translations.idiomatic: In the eighteenth year he subdued the Qipchaq after fierce fighting at Michishilao in Rus'. He then memorialized to combine the centurions of the Möngke, Naiman, Kereyid, Hanggin, and Qipchaq into a single corps.

sentences.zh: 十九年，獻馬萬匹。

translations.literal: In the nineteenth year, presented ten thousand horses.
translations.idiomatic: In the nineteenth year he presented ten thousand horses to the throne.

sentences.zh: 二十一年，取馺裏畏吾、特勤、赤憫等部，德順、鎮戎、蘭、會、洮等州，獻牝馬三千匹。

translations.literal: In the twenty-first year, took the Sariyid Uyghur, Telin, Chimin and other tribes; De Shun, Zhenrong, Lan, Hui, Tao and other prefectures; presented three thousand brood mares.
translations.idiomatic: In the twenty-first year he conquered the Sariyid Uyghurs, Telin, Chimin, and allied tribes, along with the prefectures of De Shun, Zhenrong, Lan, Hui, and Tao, and presented three thousand broodmares.

sentences.zh: 太宗二年，大舉伐金，渡河而南，睿宗以太弟將兵渡漢水而北，會河南之三峰山。

translations.literal: In the second year of Taizong, a great campaign against Jin; crossed the river southward; Ruizong as the youngest imperial brother led troops across the Han River northward; joined at Henan's Sanfeng Mountain.
translations.idiomatic: In Ögedei's second year (1230) the Mongols launched a major invasion of Jin. The main force crossed the Yellow River southward while Tolui, the youngest imperial brother, led troops north across the Han to meet at Sanfeng Mountain in Henan.

sentences.zh: 金大臣合達諸將步騎數十萬待戰，雪不臺從睿宗出牛頭關，謀曰：「城邑兵野戰不利，易破耳。」

translations.literal: Jin great ministers Hedai and various generals with infantry and cavalry several hundred thousand awaited battle; Xuebutai followed Ruizong out Ox Head Pass; schemed saying: "Walled-city troops are unfavorable in field battle—they are easy to break."
translations.idiomatic: Jin commanders led by Hedai mustered several hundred thousand infantry and cavalry to give battle. Subutai followed Tolui through Ox Head Pass and advised, "Troops tied to walled cities fare poorly in open battle—they will be easy to break."

sentences.zh: 師集三峰，金圍之數匝，將士頗懼。

translations.literal: The army gathered at Sanfeng; Jin encircled them many rounds; officers and soldiers were quite afraid.
translations.idiomatic: The Mongol force assembled at Sanfeng, where the Jin army closed around them again and again. Morale among the commanders and troops wavered.

sentences.zh: 俄而風雪大作，金卒僵踣，士氣遂奮，敵眾盡殪。

translations.literal: Suddenly wind and snow greatly arose; Jin soldiers stiffened and fell; troop spirit then soared; the enemy multitude was entirely destroyed.
translations.idiomatic: Then a great blizzard struck. Jin soldiers froze where they stood, Mongol morale surged, and the enemy host was annihilated.

sentences.zh: 河南諸州以次降破。

translations.literal: Henan various prefectures in succession surrendered or were broken.
translations.idiomatic: The prefectures of Henan fell one after another.

sentences.zh: 四年夏，雪不臺總諸道兵攻汴，金義宗走衛州，又走歸德，又走蔡州。

translations.literal: In summer of the fourth year, Xuebutai overall commanded troops of various routes to attack Bian; Jin Yizong fled to Weizhou, again fled to Guide, again fled to Caizhou.
translations.idiomatic: In the summer of the fourth year Subutai commanded the combined armies against Bian. The Jin ruler Yizong fled to Weizhou, then to Guide, and then to Caizhou.

sentences.zh: 癸巳秋，汴將以城降，其冬攻蔡。

translations.literal: In autumn of guisi, Bian's generals were about to surrender the city; that winter attacked Cai.
translations.idiomatic: In the autumn of guisi (1233) the defenders of Bian prepared to surrender the city; that winter the Mongols attacked Caizhou.

sentences.zh: 六年春，金亡。

translations.literal: In spring of the sixth year, Jin perished.
translations.idiomatic: In the spring of the sixth year the Jin dynasty fell.

sentences.zh: 雪不臺以汴民饑，縱使渡河就食，民德之。

translations.literal: Xuebutai because Bian people were famine-stricken, released them to cross the river to seek food; the people were grateful to him.
translations.idiomatic: When famine struck the people of Bian, Subutai let them cross the river to find food, and they remembered him gratefully.

sentences.zh: 是年詔宗王拔都西征，雪不臺為先鋒，戰大捷。

translations.literal: That year an edict ordered Prince Batu on the western campaign; Xuebutai was vanguard; battle was greatly victorious.
translations.idiomatic: That year Batu was ordered west on campaign, with Subutai as vanguard; he won a great victory.

sentences.zh: 十三年，討兀魯思部主野力班，禽之。

translations.literal: In the thirteenth year, punished Ulughs tribal lord Yeliban; captured him.
translations.idiomatic: In the thirteenth year he subdued Yeliban, lord of the Ulughs tribe, and took him captive.

sentences.zh: 攻馬劄部，與其酋怯憐戰漷寧河，遣偏師由下流搗其城，拔之。

translations.literal: Attacked the Majar tribe; with their chief Qielian battled at Huaning River; sent a detached column from downstream to strike their city; took it.
translations.idiomatic: Attacking the Majar tribe, he fought their chief Qielian on the Huaning River while a detached force sailed downstream to storm their city and take it.

sentences.zh: 是時，北庭、西域、河南北、關隴皆底定，雪不臺功力居多。

translations.literal: At this time, Beiting, Western Regions, north of Henan, Guan-Long—all were settled at bottom; Xuebutai's labor and merit were the greater part.
translations.idiomatic: By then Beiting, the Western Regions, north China, and Guan-Long were largely pacified, and Subutai's contribution was the greatest among the generals.

sentences.zh: 初，太祖征西夏，閔其久於行間，敕還省覲。

translations.literal: Initially, Taizu campaigning against Western Xia, pitying his long time in the ranks, ordered him to return and visit family.
translations.idiomatic: Early in the Western Xia campaign, Genghis Khan, pitying Subutai's long years in the field, ordered him home to see his family.

sentences.zh: 雪不臺對曰：「君勞臣佚，情所未安。」

translations.literal: Xuebutai replied saying: "The lord toils while the minister rests—in feeling this is not yet at ease."
translations.idiomatic: Subutai replied, "When the lord toils and the minister rests, my heart cannot be at ease."

sentences.zh: 帝壯而聽之。

translations.literal: The Emperor approved and listened to him.
translations.idiomatic: The Khan admired this and allowed him to remain.

sentences.zh: 又金帥合達見獲，以不屈死，猶問雪不臺安在，請一識之。

translations.literal: Also Jin commander Hedai was captured; because he would not submit he died; still asked where Xuebutai was; requested once to know him.
translations.idiomatic: When the captured Jin commander Hedai, who chose death rather than submission, still asked where Subutai was and begged to see him once.

sentences.zh: 雪不臺出謂曰：「汝須臾人耳，識我何為？」

translations.literal: Xuebutai came out and said to him: "You are a man of a brief moment—what is the use of knowing me?"
translations.idiomatic: Subutai came forward and said, "You are a man with little time left—why wish to know me?"

sentences.zh: 曰：「人臣亦各為其主，卿勇蓋諸將，天生英豪，其偶然邪。

translations.literal: He said: "Ministers each also serve their lord; your courage covers all generals; heaven-born heroic talent—is it by chance?
translations.idiomatic: Hedai said, "Every minister serves his own lord. Your valor surpasses all the generals—surely you are a hero born of heaven, not chance alone.

sentences.zh: 吾見卿，甘心瞑目矣。」

translations.literal: Having seen you, I am willing at heart to close my eyes in death."
translations.idiomatic: To have seen you, I can close my eyes content."

sentences.zh: 定宗三年，卒於篤列河之地，年七十有三。

translations.literal: In the third year of Dingzong, he died at the place of Dölei River; age seventy-three.
translations.idiomatic: In the third year of Güyük (1248), he died on the Dölei River at the age of seventy-three.

sentences.zh: 至大元年，贈效忠宣力佐命功臣、開府儀同三司、上柱國、河南王，謚忠定。

translations.literal: In the first year of Zhida, posthumously granted Loyal and Effort-displaying Merit-assisting Mandate Meritorious Minister, Grand Master of the Palace with Grand Prefecture and Three Excellencies rank, Upper Pillar of State, King of Henan; posthumous title Zhongding.
translations.idiomatic: In Zhida 1 (1308) he was posthumously ennobled as Loyal Merit-Assisting Minister, Grand Master of the Palace of the First Rank, Upper Pillar of State, and King of Henan, with the posthumous name Zhongding ("Loyal and Steadfast").

sentences.zh: ○唵木海

translations.literal: ○ Anmuhai
translations.idiomatic: ○ Anmuhai

sentences.zh: 至元十年，修立正陽東西二城，置炮二百餘座，與宋人戰，卻之。

translations.literal: In the tenth year of Zhiyuan, repaired and established the eastern and western cities of Zhengyang; set up more than two hundred artillery emplacements; battled Song people; repelled them.
translations.idiomatic: In Zhiyuan 10 (1273) he built the eastern and western fortresses at Zhengyang, emplaced more than two hundred artillery pieces, fought the Song, and drove them back.

sentences.zh: 十三年，從丞相伯顏伐宋，駐軍臨安之阜亭山，同忙古歹等八人率甲三百入宋宮，取傳國寶。

translations.literal: In the thirteenth year, followed Chancellor Bayan campaigning against Song; encamped army at Futing Mountain near Lin'an; together with Mangudai and eight others led three hundred armored men into the Song palace; took the imperial transmission seal.
translations.idiomatic: In 1276 he followed Chancellor Bayan against the Song. The army encamped at Futing Mountain outside Lin'an; with Mangudai and seven others he led three hundred armored men into the Song palace to seize the imperial seal of transmission.

sentences.zh: 宋太后請解兵延見內殿，期明日奉寶乞降，至期，果遣賈余慶等奉寶至軍前。

translations.literal: Song empress dowager requested dismissing troops and extending audience in the inner hall; arranged tomorrow to present the treasure and beg surrender; when the date arrived, indeed sent Jia Yuqing and others to present the treasure before the army.
translations.idiomatic: The Song empress dowager asked that hostilities cease and received them in the inner palace, promising to deliver the seal and sue for peace the next day. On the appointed day Jia Yuqing and others duly brought the seal to the Mongol camp.

sentences.zh: 以功授行省斷事官，復令其子忽都答兒襲炮手總管。

translations.literal: For merit he was appointed Branch Secretariat judicial officer; again ordered his son Hududar to inherit artillery commander-general.
translations.idiomatic: For his service he was made a judicial officer of the branch secretariat, and his son Hududar was appointed to succeed him as commander of the artillery corps.

sentences.zh: 十四年，進昭勇大將軍炮手萬戶，佩元降虎符，鎮平江之常熟。

translations.literal: In the fourteenth year, advanced to General of Manifest Courage, artillery myriarch; wore Yuan surrender tiger tally; guarded Changshu in Pingjiang.
translations.idiomatic: In the fourteenth year he was promoted to General of Manifest Courage and artillery myriarch, given a tiger tally, and posted to Changshu in Pingjiang.

sentences.zh: 有叛民擁眾自號太尉者，行省會諸軍討之，與忽都答兒父子自為一軍，奮戈陷陣，斬賊酋戴太尉，擒朱太尉，帝嘉其功。

translations.literal: There were rebel people gathering a multitude self-styling themselves Grand Commandant; the branch secretariat assembled various armies to punish them; with Hududar father and son forming their own army; they vigorously wielded spears breaking formations; beheaded rebel chief Dai Taiwei; captured Zhu Taiwei; the Emperor commended their merit.
translations.idiomatic: When rebels styling themselves "Grand Commandant" gathered in force, the branch secretariat mustered troops to crush them. Anmuhai and Hududar led their own unit, fought through the enemy lines, beheaded the rebel chief Dai Taiwei, captured Zhu Taiwei, and the Emperor praised their achievement.

sentences.zh: 十五年，兼平江路達魯花赤，尋遷徽州、湖州，卒。

translations.literal: In the fifteenth year, concurrently Pingjiang Route darughachi; soon transferred to Huizhou and Huzhou; died.
translations.idiomatic: In the fifteenth year he also served as darughachi of Pingjiang Route, then was transferred to Huizhou and Huzhou, where he died.

sentences.zh: 忽都答兒後升炮手萬戶，改授達魯花赤，卒。

translations.literal: Hududar afterward was promoted artillery myriarch; changed appointment to darughachi; died.
translations.idiomatic: Hududar was later promoted to artillery myriarch and then appointed darughachi; he too died in office.

sentences.zh: ○昔裏鈐部

translations.literal: ○ Xiliqianbu
translations.idiomatic: ○ Xiliqianbu

sentences.zh: 昔裏鈐部，唐兀人，昔裏氏。

translations.literal: Xiliqianbu, a Tangut person, of the Xili clan.
translations.idiomatic: Xiliqianbu was a Tangut of the Xili clan.

sentences.zh: 鈐部亦云甘卜，音相近而互用也。

translations.literal: Qianbu is also called Ganbu; the sounds are near and used interchangeably.
translations.idiomatic: Qianbu was also called Ganbu—the names were close in sound and used interchangeably.

sentences.zh: 太祖時，西夏既臣服，大軍西征，復懷貳心。

translations.literal: In Taizu's time, Western Xia having already submitted, when the great army campaigned west they again harbored double hearts.
translations.idiomatic: Under Genghis Khan, after Western Xia had submitted, they showed disloyalty again when the main army marched west.

sentences.zh: 帝聞之，旋師致討。

translations.literal: The Emperor heard this; turned the army back to deliver punishment.
translations.idiomatic: Hearing of this, the Khan wheeled his army around to punish them.

sentences.zh: 命鈐部同忽都鐵穆兒招諭沙州。

translations.literal: Ordered Qianbu together with Qudu Tiemu'er to summon and persuade Shazhou.
translations.idiomatic: He ordered Qianbu and Qudu Tiemu'er to summon Shazhou to surrender.

sentences.zh: 州將偽降，以牛酒犒師，而設伏兵以待之。

translations.literal: The prefecture general feigned surrender; with cattle and wine feasted the army; yet set hidden troops waiting for them.
translations.idiomatic: The prefecture commander feigned submission, sent oxen and wine to entertain the army, and laid an ambush.

sentences.zh: 首帥至，伏發馬躓，鈐部以所乘馬與首帥使奔，自乘所躓馬而殿後，擊敗之。

translations.literal: When the chief commander arrived, the ambush sprang and horses stumbled; Qianbu gave his own mount to the chief commander enabling flight; himself rode the stumbled horse and brought up the rear; defeated them.
translations.idiomatic: When the commander arrived the ambush struck and horses stumbled. Qianbu gave his own mount to the commander to escape, himself took a faltering horse and fought in the rear until the enemy was beaten off.

sentences.zh: 他日，帝聞曰：「卿臨死地，而易馬與人，何也？」

translations.literal: Another day, the Emperor heard and said: "You facing death's ground, yet exchanged horses and gave to another—why?"
translations.idiomatic: Later the Khan asked, "You were in mortal peril—why give your horse to another?"

sentences.zh: 鈐部對曰：「小臣陣死，不足重輕，首帥乃陛下器使宿將，不可失也。」

translations.literal: Qianbu replied saying: "This petty minister dying in battle is not enough to weigh light or heavy; the chief commander is Your Majesty's appointed veteran general—he must not be lost."
translations.idiomatic: Qianbu answered, "My death in battle would matter little; the commander is a seasoned general of Your Majesty's—he must not be lost."

sentences.zh: 帝以為忠。

translations.literal: The Emperor regarded it as loyalty.
translations.idiomatic: The Khan took this as proof of loyalty.

sentences.zh: 進兵圍肅州，守者乃鈐部之兄，懼城破害及其家，先以為請。

translations.literal: Advancing troops to surround Suzhou; the defender was Qianbu's elder brother; fearing the city would fall and harm would reach his family, he first made this request.
translations.idiomatic: The army advanced to besiege Suzhou. The city's defender was Qianbu's elder brother; fearing that once the walls fell his family would be slaughtered, he pleaded for their lives beforehand.

sentences.zh: 帝怒城久不下，有旨盡屠之，惟聽鈐部求其親族家人於死所，於是得免死者百有六戶，歸其田業。

translations.literal: The Emperor, angered that the city long did not fall, issued an edict to slaughter all; only allowed Qianbu to seek his kin and household members at the place of death; thereby were spared one hundred and six households, and their fields and estates were returned.
translations.idiomatic: Angry at the long siege, the Khan ordered that the city be put entirely to the sword—yet permitted Qianbu alone to claim his kin at the slaughter. One hundred and six households were spared, and their fields restored.

sentences.zh: 歲乙未，定宗、憲宗皆以親王與速卜帶征西域，明年啟行，鈐部亦在中。

translations.literal: In the yiwei year, Emperor Dingzong and Emperor Xianzong both as imperial princes with Subutai campaigned to the Western Regions; the next year they set out; Qianbu was among them.
translations.idiomatic: In the yiwei year (1235), both Ögedei and Möngke, still princes, joined Subutai's western campaign. When the army marched the following year, Qianbu was in their ranks.

sentences.zh: 又明年，至寬田吉思海，鈐部從諸王拔都征斡羅斯，至也裏贊城，大戰七日，拔之。

translations.literal: Again the next year, reaching Lake Qarachoq; Qianbu followed Prince Batu campaigning against Rus; reaching Yaroslavl city, great battle seven days, captured it.
translations.idiomatic: The year after that they reached Lake Qarachoq. Qianbu followed Batu against Rus as far as Yaroslavl, where after seven days of hard fighting the city was taken.

sentences.zh: 己亥冬十有一月，至阿速滅怯思城，負固久不下。

translations.literal: In jihai, winter, eleventh month, reaching the city of Asuq Mekes, they held firm stubbornly long unable to capture.
translations.idiomatic: In the eleventh month of winter in the jihai year (1239), they came to Asuq Mekes, which held out stubbornly and would not fall.

sentences.zh: 明年春正月，鈐部率敢死士十人，躡雲梯先登，俘十一人，大呼曰：「城破矣！」

translations.literal: Next year spring first month, Qianbu led ten dare-death warriors, following cloud-ladders first ascending, captured eleven men, loudly shouting saying: "The city is broken!"
translations.idiomatic: In the first month of the following spring, Qianbu led ten volunteers up the siege ladders ahead of all others, took eleven captives, and cried, "The wall is breached!"

sentences.zh: 眾蟻附而上，遂拔之。

translations.literal: The multitude like ants attached and ascended; then captured it.
translations.idiomatic: The rest swarmed up after him like ants on a mound, and the city fell.

sentences.zh: 賜西馬、西錦，錫名拔都。

translations.literal: Granted Western horses, Western brocade; bestowed the name Batu.
translations.idiomatic: He was rewarded with horses and brocade from the west, and granted the name Batu ("Hero").

sentences.zh: 明年班師，授鈐部千戶，賜只孫為四時宴服，尋遷斷事官。

translations.literal: Next year the army returned; appointed Qianbu chiliarch; granted jeun as feast robes for four seasons; soon transferred to judge-official.
translations.idiomatic: When the army returned the next year, Qianbu was made a chiliarch, given ceremonial robes for court, and soon appointed a judge.

sentences.zh: 丙午，定宗即位，進秩大名路達魯花赤。

translations.literal: In bingwu, Dingzong succeeded the throne; promoted rank to Daming Route darughachi.
translations.idiomatic: In the bingwu year (1246), when Ögedei took the throne, Qianbu was promoted to darughachi of Daming Route.

sentences.zh: 憲宗以卜只兒來蒞行臺，命鈐部同署，既又別錫虎符，出監大名。

translations.literal: Xianzong sent Bojier to come direct the branch secretariat; ordered Qianbu to jointly administer; then separately bestowed tiger tally; went out to oversee Daming.
translations.idiomatic: Möngke sent Bojier to head the branch secretariat and had Qianbu serve alongside him; Qianbu was later given a separate tiger tally and sent to oversee Daming.

sentences.zh: 己未，世祖南征，供給軍餉，未嘗乏絕。

translations.literal: In jiwei, Shizu campaigned south; supplied army provisions, never once lacked or exhausted.
translations.idiomatic: During Kublai's southern campaigns in the jiwei year (1259), Qianbu kept the army supplied without fail.

sentences.zh: 以疾輿歸，卒於家，年六十九。

translations.literal: Due to illness carried in litter home; died at home; age sixty-nine.
translations.idiomatic: He fell ill and was carried home, where he died at sixty-nine.

sentences.zh: 子愛魯。

translations.literal: Son Ailu.
translations.idiomatic: His son was Ailu.

sentences.zh: 愛魯襲為大名路達魯花赤。

translations.literal: Ailu inherited as Daming Route darughachi.
translations.idiomatic: Ailu succeeded him as darughachi of Daming Route.

sentences.zh: 至元五年，從雲南王征金齒諸部。

translations.literal: In the fifth year of Zhiyuan, followed the Prince of Yunnan campaigning against the Gold Teeth various tribes.
translations.idiomatic: In 1268 he joined the Prince of Yunnan's campaign against the Gold Teeth tribes.

sentences.zh: 蠻兵萬人絕縹甸道，擊之，斬首千餘級，諸部震服。

translations.literal: Barbarian troops ten thousand cut off the Piaodian route; attacked them; beheaded more than a thousand heads; the various tribes trembled and submitted.
translations.idiomatic: Ten thousand tribal warriors blocked the Piaodian route; he attacked, slew more than a thousand, and the tribes submitted in awe.

sentences.zh: 六年，再入，定其租賦，平火不麻等二十四寨，得七馴象以還。

translations.literal: Sixth year, entered again; fixed their rent and tax; pacified Huobuma and other twenty-four stockades; obtained seven trained elephants and returned.
translations.idiomatic: In the sixth year he returned, fixed their taxes, pacified twenty-four stockades including Huobuma, and came back with seven trained elephants.

sentences.zh: 七年，改中慶路達魯花赤，兼管爨僰軍。

translations.literal: Seventh year, changed to Zhongqing Route darughachi; concurrently administered Cuanbo armies.
translations.idiomatic: In the seventh year he was made darughachi of Zhongqing Route and given charge of the Cuanbo troops.

sentences.zh: 十年，平章賽典赤行省雲南，令愛魯疆理永昌，增田為多。

translations.literal: Tenth year, Pingzhang Saidianchi administered Yunnan branch secretariat; ordered Ailu to extend and put in order Yongchang; increased fields to much.
translations.idiomatic: In 1273, when Saidianchi was governing Yunnan, Ailu was put in charge of Yongchang and greatly expanded the arable land.

sentences.zh: 十一年，閱中慶版籍，得隱戶萬餘，以四千戶即其地屯田。

translations.literal: Eleventh year, examined Zhongqing register rolls; obtained hidden households more than ten thousand; with four thousand households immediately at that land established garrison fields.
translations.idiomatic: In the eleventh year he audited Zhongqing's registers, found more than ten thousand concealed households, and settled four thousand of them on local garrison farms.

sentences.zh: 十三年，詔開烏蒙道，帥師至玉連等州，所過城寨，未附者盡擊下之，水陸皆置驛傳，由是大為賽典赤信任。

translations.literal: Thirteenth year, edict to open Wumeng route; led troops reaching Yulian and other prefectures; every stockade passed through not yet attached was all struck and taken down; by water and land all established relay stations; thereby greatly gained Saidianchi's trust.
translations.idiomatic: In 1276, ordered to open the Wumeng route, he led troops through Yulian and other prefectures, reduced every holdout along the way, established relay posts by land and water, and thereby won Saidianchi's full confidence.

sentences.zh: 十四年，忙部、也可不薛叛，以兵二千討平之，遷廣南西道左右兩江宣撫使，兼招討使。

translations.literal: Fourteenth year, Mangbu and Yeke Buqie rebelled; with troops two thousand suppressed and pacified them; transferred to Guangnan West Circuit Left and Right Two Rivers appeasement commissioner, concurrently pacification commissioner.
translations.idiomatic: In 1277, when Mangbu and Yeke Buqie rebelled, he put them down with two thousand men and was made appeasement commissioner of the Two Rivers in western Guangnan, with the added title of pacification commissioner.

sentences.zh: 十六年，遷雲南諸路宣慰使、副都元帥。

translations.literal: Sixteenth year, transferred to Yunnan various circuits pacification commissioner, vice grand marshal.
translations.idiomatic: In the sixteenth year he became pacification commissioner of all Yunnan circuits and vice grand marshal.

sentences.zh: 十七年，復立雲南行省，拜參知政事。

translations.literal: Seventeenth year, re-established Yunnan branch secretariat; appointed vice director of the Secretariat.
translations.idiomatic: When the Yunnan branch secretariat was reestablished in the seventeenth year, he was made vice director of the Secretariat.

sentences.zh: 十八年，烏蒙羅佐山，白水江蠻殺萬戶阿忽以叛，復討平之。

translations.literal: Eighteenth year, at Wumeng Luozuo Mountain, Baishuijiang barbarians killed Myriarch Ahu and rebelled; again campaigned and pacified them.
