translations.idiomatic: In 1281, tribes on Luozuo Mountain in Wumeng killed Myriarch Ahu and rose in revolt; Ailu campaigned and crushed them again.

sentences.zh: 十九年，召詣闕，進左丞。

translations.literal: Nineteenth year, summoned to approach the court; promoted to left vice director.
translations.idiomatic: In 1282 he was summoned to court and promoted to left vice director.

sentences.zh: 也可不薛復叛，詔與西川都元帥也速答兒、湖南行省脫裏察會師進討，禽也可不薛送京師，仁普諸酋長皆降，得戶四千。

translations.literal: Yeke Buqie again rebelled; edict with Sichuan grand marshal Yesu Da'er, Hunan branch secretariat Tuolicha to join forces and advance to punish; captured Yeke Buqie and sent to the capital; Renpu and various chieftains all surrendered; obtained four thousand households.
translations.idiomatic: When Yeke Buqie rebelled again, Ailu was ordered to join Grand Marshal Yesu Da'er of Sichuan and Tuolicha of Hunan in a joint campaign. Yeke Buqie was captured and sent to the capital; chiefs of Renpu and other districts submitted, yielding four thousand households.

sentences.zh: 諸王相吾答兒帥諸將征緬，愛魯供饋餉，無乏絕。

translations.literal: Prince Sang'u Da'er commanded various generals campaigning against Burma; Ailu supplied provisions, without lack or exhaustion.
translations.idiomatic: When Prince Sang'u Da'er led generals against Burma, Ailu kept the supply lines full without interruption.

sentences.zh: 二十二年，烏蒙阿謀殺宣撫使以叛，與右丞拜答兒往征之，拜答兒以愛魯習知其山川道里，令諸軍悉聽指授，分道進擊，生擒阿蒙以歸。

translations.literal: Twenty-second year, Wumeng A'Mou killed the appeasement commissioner and rebelled; with right vice director Baidu'er went to campaign; Baidu'er because Ailu was skilled knowing the mountains rivers routes and distances, ordered all armies entirely obey his command and direction; divided routes advancing to attack; captured alive A'Meng and returned.
translations.idiomatic: In 1285, when A'Mou of Wumeng killed the appeasement commissioner and rebelled, Ailu marched with Vice Director Baidu'er. Knowing Ailu's mastery of the terrain, Baidu'er placed all troops under his direction; the force split into columns, captured A'Mou alive, and returned.

sentences.zh: 二十四年，進右丞。

translations.literal: Twenty-fourth year, promoted to right vice director.
translations.idiomatic: In 1287 he was promoted to right vice director.

sentences.zh: 朝廷立尚書省，復改行尚書右丞。

translations.literal: The court established the Department of State Affairs; again changed to acting right vice director of the Department.
translations.idiomatic: When the Department of State Affairs was established, he was made acting right vice director of that branch.

sentences.zh: 鎮南王征交趾，詔愛魯將兵六千人從之。

translations.literal: Prince of Zhennan campaigned against Jiaozhi; edict Ailu to lead troops six thousand to follow.
translations.idiomatic: When the Prince of Zhennan invaded Annam, Ailu was ordered to follow with six thousand men.

sentences.zh: 自羅羅至交趾境，交趾將昭文王以兵四萬守木兀門，愛魯與戰破之，擒其將黎石、何英。

translations.literal: From Luoluo to Jiaozhi border, Jiaozhi general Zhaowen Wang with troops forty thousand guarded Mu'ermen; Ailu fought and broke them; captured their generals Li Shi and He Ying.
translations.idiomatic: From Luoluo to the Annam frontier, Annam's Prince Zhaowen defended Mu'ermen Pass with forty thousand men. Ailu broke the force and captured the generals Li Shi and He Ying.

sentences.zh: 比三月，大小一十八戰，乃至其王城，與諸軍會戰又二十餘合，功為多。

translations.literal: By the third month, great and small eighteen battles; then reaching their royal city; with all armies joined battle again more than twenty rounds; merit was foremost.
translations.idiomatic: Within three months he fought eighteen engagements, reached the royal capital, and in more than twenty pitched battles with the main force contributed the greatest share of the victories.

sentences.zh: 二十五年，感瘴癘卒。

translations.literal: Twenty-fifth year, succumbed to miasma pestilence and died.
translations.idiomatic: In 1288 he died of pestilence in the southern marshes.

sentences.zh: 贈平章政事，謚毅敏。

translations.literal: Posthumously granted pingzhang political affairs; posthumous name Yimin.
translations.idiomatic: He was posthumously honored as a grand councilor with the posthumous name Yi-min ("Resolute and Keen").

sentences.zh: 子教化，中書平章政事，請於朝，贈其祖昔裏鈐部太師，謚貞獻，加贈愛魯太師，追封魏國公，改謚忠節。

translations.literal: Son Jiaohua, Secretariat pingzhang political affairs; requested at court; posthumously granted his grandfather Xili Qianbu Grand Preceptor, posthumous name Zhenxian; additionally posthumously granted Ailu Grand Preceptor; retroactively enfeoffed as Duke of Wei, changed posthumous name to Zhongjie.
translations.idiomatic: His son Jiaohua, a grand councilor of the Secretariat, petitioned the court to posthumously honor his grandfather Xiliqianbu as Grand Preceptor with the title Zhenxian, and to grant Ailu the additional posthumous rank of Grand Preceptor, the title Duke of Wei, and the name Zhongjie ("Loyal unto Death").

sentences.zh: ○槊直腯魯華

translations.literal: ○ Shuozhituluhua
translations.idiomatic: ○ Shuozhituluhua

sentences.zh: 槊直腯魯華，蒙古克烈氏。

translations.literal: Shuozhituluhua, Mongol of the Kerait clan.
translations.idiomatic: Shuozhituluhua was a Mongol of the Kerait clan.

sentences.zh: 初，以其部人二百從太祖征乃蠻、西夏有功，命將萬人，為太師國王木華黎前鋒。

translations.literal: At first, with two hundred men of his tribe following Taizu campaigning against Naiman and Western Xia with merit; ordered to command ten thousand; served as Grand Preceptor King Muqali's vanguard.
translations.idiomatic: Early on he led two hundred tribesmen under Genghis Khan against the Naiman and Western Xia with distinction, was given command of ten thousand, and served as vanguard to King Muqali.

sentences.zh: 下金桓州，得其監馬幾百萬匹，分屬諸軍，軍勢大振。

translations.literal: Took Jin Huan Prefecture; obtained their supervised horses several million head; divided and assigned to various armies; army momentum greatly revived.
translations.idiomatic: After taking Jin Huan Prefecture he seized several million horses from the royal stud, distributed them among the armies, and the army's strength surged.

sentences.zh: 歲辛未，破遼東、西諸州，唯東京未下，獲金使，遣往諭之。

translations.literal: In the xinwei year, broke Liaodong and western various prefectures; only Eastern Capital not yet taken; captured a Jin envoy; sent him to persuade them.
translations.idiomatic: In the xinwei year (1211) he overran the eastern and western prefectures of Liaodong; only Dongjing held out. A Jin envoy was captured and sent to urge its surrender.

sentences.zh: 槊直腯魯華曰：「東京，金舊都，備嚴而守固，攻之未易下，以計破之可也。

translations.literal: Shuozhituluhua said: "Eastern Capital, Jin's former capital, prepared strictly and defended solidly; attacking it not easy to take—by stratagem to break it is possible.
translations.idiomatic: Shuozhituluhua said, "Dongjing was the Jin old capital—heavily fortified and not easily stormed. It can be taken by ruse.

sentences.zh: 請易服與其使偕往說之，彼將不疑，俟其門開，繼以大軍赴之，則可克矣。」

translations.literal: Request to change clothes and with their envoy together go persuade them; they will not suspect; wait until their gate opens; follow with great army rushing thereto; then can capture it."
translations.idiomatic: Let me change clothes and go with their envoy to parley—they will not suspect us. When the gates open, the main army can rush in and the city will fall."

sentences.zh: 卒如其計。

translations.literal: In the end as his plan.
translations.idiomatic: It worked exactly as he had planned.

sentences.zh: 徇地河北，攻大名，小大數十戰，城垂陷，中流矢而卒。

translations.literal: Subduing lands in Hebei; attacked Daming; great and small several tens of battles; city nearly fallen; struck by arrow mid-stream and died.
translations.idiomatic: Advancing through Hebei, he assaulted Daming in dozens of engagements. The city was nearly his when he was struck by an arrow and died.

sentences.zh: 武宗時，贈太傅，追封衛國公，謚武敏。

translations.literal: In Wuzong's time, posthumously granted Grand Tutor; retroactively enfeoffed Duke of Weiguo; posthumous name Wumin.
translations.idiomatic: Under the Wuzong emperor he was posthumously made Grand Tutor, enfeoffed as Duke of Weiguo, with the posthumous name Wu-min ("Martial and Keen").

sentences.zh: 子撒吉思卜華，嗣將其軍。

translations.literal: Son Sagisibuhua, succeeded commanding his army.
translations.idiomatic: His son Sagisibuhua succeeded to command of his troops.

sentences.zh: 太宗元年己丑，錫金符，安輯河北、山東諸州。

translations.literal: First year of Taizong jichou, granted gold tally; pacified and comforted Hebei and Shandong various prefectures.
translations.idiomatic: In the first year of Ögedei's reign (1229), he received a gold tally and was charged with pacifying the prefectures of Hebei and Shandong.

sentences.zh: 先是真定同知武仙攻滅都元帥史天倪家，其弟天澤擊仙走，復真定。

translations.literal: Earlier, Zhending vice prefect Wu Xian attacked and destroyed Metropolitan General Shi Tianni's household; his younger brother Tianze struck Xian and drove him off; recovered Zhending.
translations.idiomatic: Earlier, Wu Xian, vice prefect of Zhending, had overrun Metropolitan General Shi Tianni's household; Tianni's brother Tianze routed Wu Xian and recovered the city.

sentences.zh: 以天澤為真定、河間、濟南、東平、大名五路萬戶。

translations.literal: Made Tianze myriarch of five circuits Zhending, Hejian, Jinan, Dongping, Daming.
translations.idiomatic: Shi Tianze was made myriarch over the five circuits of Zhending, Hejian, Jinan, Dongping, and Daming.

sentences.zh: 庚寅，命撒吉思卜華佩金虎符，以總師行省監其軍。

translations.literal: In gengyin, ordered Sagisibuhua to wear the gold tiger tally; to command the army, branch secretariat oversee his troops.
translations.idiomatic: In the gengyin year (1230) Sagisibuhua was given a gold tiger tally and placed in overall command with branch secretariat oversight of Shi Tianze's army.

sentences.zh: 金宣宗之徙都於汴也，立河平軍於新衛以自固，恃為北門。

translations.literal: When Jin Emperor Xuanzong moved the capital to Bian, established He Ping Army at Xinwei to strengthen himself; relied on it as northern gate.
translations.idiomatic: When Emperor Xuanzong of Jin moved his capital to Kaifeng, he stationed the He Ping Army at Xinwei as his northern bulwark.

sentences.zh: 撒吉思卜華數攻之，不拔。

translations.literal: Sagisibuhua several times attacked it; could not take.
translations.idiomatic: Sagisibuhua attacked it repeatedly without success.

sentences.zh: 壬辰正月，太宗自白坡濟河而南，睿宗由峭石灘涉漢而北。

translations.literal: In renchen first month, Taizong from Baipo crossed the river southward; Ruizong from Qiaoshi Tan forded the Han northward.
translations.idiomatic: In the first month of renchen (1232), Ögedei crossed the Yellow River south from Baipo while Tolui forded the Han from Qiaoshi Tan in the north.

sentences.zh: 撒吉思卜華集西都水之舟，渡自河陰。

translations.literal: Sagisibuhua assembled boats of the western capital's waters; crossed from Heyin.
translations.idiomatic: Sagisibuhua gathered boats on the Western Capital's rivers and crossed from Heyin.

sentences.zh: 至鄭，鄭守馬伯堅降。

translations.literal: Reached Zheng; Zheng defender Ma Bojian surrendered.
translations.idiomatic: At Zhengzhou, the commander Ma Bojian surrendered.

sentences.zh: 及金義宗勢力窮蹙出奔，帝命撒吉思卜華追躡之，會其節度斜撚阿卜棄衛入汴，撒吉思卜華遂據而有之。

translations.literal: When Jin Emperor Yizong's power was exhausted and cornered and fled, the Emperor ordered Sagisibuhua to pursue; meeting their commissioner Xienian Abu abandon Xinwei and enter Bian, Sagisibuhua then occupied and possessed it.
translations.idiomatic: When Emperor Yizong of Jin was driven to flight, the Khan ordered Sagisibuhua in pursuit. The Jin commissioner Xienian Abu abandoned Xinwei and fled to Kaifeng, and Sagisibuhua took the city.

sentences.zh: 十二月，義宗自黃陵岡濟河，謀復衛。

translations.literal: Twelfth month, Yizong from Huangling Gang crossed the river; plotted to recover Xinwei.
translations.idiomatic: In the twelfth month Emperor Yizong crossed from Huangling Gang, intending to retake Xinwei.

sentences.zh: 撒吉思卜華與其將白撒戰白公廟五日夜，俘斬萬計，余眾盡潰。

translations.literal: Sagisibuhua with his general Baisa fought at Baigong Temple five days and nights; captured and beheaded tens of thousands; remaining masses all routed.
translations.idiomatic: At Baigong Temple, Sagisibuhua and his general Baisa fought for five days and nights, killing and capturing tens of thousands until the remnant army broke and fled.

sentences.zh: 義宗竄歸德。

translations.literal: Yizong fled in hiding to Guide.
translations.idiomatic: Emperor Yizong fled to Guide.

sentences.zh: 撒吉思卜華追躡其後，薄北門而軍。

translations.literal: Sagisibuhua pursued close behind; pressed to the north gate and encamped.
translations.idiomatic: Sagisibuhua pressed close behind and camped beneath the north gate.

sentences.zh: 左右皆水，其舟師日至。

translations.literal: Left and right all water; their naval forces daily arrived.
translations.idiomatic: Water hemmed him in on every side while his river fleet grew daily.

sentences.zh: 癸巳四月，其將官奴夜來斫營，腹背受敵，撒吉思卜華與一軍皆沒。

translations.literal: In guisi fourth month, their general Guannu by night came to chop the camp; received enemies belly and back; Sagisibuhua together with one army all perished.
translations.idiomatic: In the fourth month of guisi (1233), the Jin general Guannu raided by night; caught between two fires, Sagisibuhua and his whole army were destroyed.

sentences.zh: 嗣國王塔思承制，以其弟明安答兒領其行營，尋有旨以為蒙古漢軍萬戶。

translations.literal: Successor King Tasi received commission; with his younger brother Mingandai'er led his field camp; soon had edict making him Mongol and Han army myriarch.
translations.idiomatic: King Tasi, who succeeded the kingship, appointed his brother Mingandai'er to lead the camp; soon an edict made Mingandai'er myriarch of the Mongol-Han army.

sentences.zh: 明安答兒善騎射，從征淮安，因糧於敵，未嘗匱乏，軍士免負擔之勞，咸樂為用。

translations.literal: Mingandai'er skilled at mounted archery; followed campaigning at Huai'an; drew grain from the enemy; never once lacked; soldiers spared burden-carrying toil; all gladly served under him.
translations.idiomatic: Mingandai'er excelled in horsemanship and archery. On campaign at Huai'an he foraged from the enemy and never ran short, so his men were spared heavy loads and served him willingly.

sentences.zh: 癸丑，憲宗遣從昔烈門太子南伐，死於鈞州。

translations.literal: In guichou, Xianzong sent him following Prince Shiremen south to attack; died at Jun Prefecture.
translations.idiomatic: In guichou (1253), sent by Möngke to follow Prince Shiremen on the southern campaign, he died at Junzhou.

sentences.zh: 五子，長腯虎，幼普闌溪。

translations.literal: Five sons; eldest Tuhu; youngest Pulanci.
translations.idiomatic: He had five sons—the eldest Tuhu and the youngest Pulanci.

sentences.zh: 腯虎從世祖北征叛王，挺戈出入其陣，帝壯之，賜號拔都，賞白金四百五十兩。

translations.literal: Tuhu followed Shizu north campaigning against rebel princes; levelled spear entering and exiting their formations; the Emperor admired him; granted the title Batu; rewarded white gold four hundred fifty liang.
translations.idiomatic: Tuhu followed Kublai against the rebel princes in the north, thrusting spear through their ranks. The Khan admired his courage, granted him the name Batu, and rewarded him with four hundred and fifty taels of silver.

sentences.zh: 及平李亶之亂，亦有戰功。

translations.literal: When pacifying Li Tan's rebellion, also had battle merit.
translations.idiomatic: He also distinguished himself in putting down Li Tan's rebellion.

sentences.zh: 普闌溪，光祿大夫、徽政使。

translations.literal: Pulanci, Grand Master for Splendid Happiness, commissioner of the Office of Imperial Regalia.
translations.idiomatic: Pulanci served as Grand Master for Splendid Happiness and commissioner of the Office of Imperial Regalia.

sentences.zh: 金亡，命大臣忽都虎料民分封功臣，撒吉思卜華妻楊氏自陳曰：「吾舅及夫皆死國事，而獨爾見遺。」

translations.literal: When Jin perished, ordered great minister Quduhu to assess people and distribute enfeoffments to meritorious ministers; Sagisibuhua's wife Lady Yang herself stated saying: "My uncle-in-law and husband both died for the state's affairs, yet you alone are overlooked."
translations.idiomatic: After the fall of Jin, when minister Quduhu was assigned to register subjects and reward the meritorious, Sagisibuhua's widow Lady Yang pleaded: "My uncle-in-law and husband both died for the state, yet our house alone is passed over."

sentences.zh: 事聞，帝曰：「彼家再世死難，宜賜新衛民二百戶。」

translations.literal: Matter heard; the Emperor said: "That family twice generations died in calamity; ought to grant Xinwei people two hundred households."
translations.idiomatic: When the Khan heard of it he said, "That house has lost two generations in battle; grant them two hundred households from Xinwei."

sentences.zh: 撒吉思卜華贈太師，謚忠武。

translations.literal: Sagisibuhua posthumously granted Grand Preceptor; posthumous name Zhongwu.
translations.idiomatic: Sagisibuhua was posthumously honored as Grand Preceptor with the name Zhongwu ("Loyal and Martial").

sentences.zh: 明安答兒贈太保，謚武毅，爵皆衛國公。

translations.literal: Mingandai'er posthumously granted Grand Guardian; posthumous name Wuyi; both ranks Duke of Weiguo.
translations.idiomatic: Mingandai'er was posthumously made Grand Guardian with the name Wuyi ("Martial and Resolute"); both were enfeoffed as Dukes of Weiguo.

sentences.zh: ○昔兒吉思

translations.literal: ○ Xi'erjisi
translations.idiomatic: ○ Xi'erjisi

sentences.zh: 昔兒吉思，幼從太祖征回回、河西諸國，俱有戰功。

translations.literal: Xi'erjisi, from youth followed Taizu campaigning against Muslim and Hexi various states; all had battle merit.
translations.idiomatic: Xi'erjisi had followed Genghis Khan from youth in campaigns against the Muslim lands and the Hexi states, winning distinction in each.

sentences.zh: 太宗時，從睿宗西征，師次京兆府，會亦來哈<角┦>率諸部兵作亂，昔兒吉思挺身斫賊陣，下馬搏戰，賊眾莫不披靡。

translations.literal: In Taizong's time, followed Ruizong west campaigning; army halted at Jingzhao Prefecture; meeting Yilahudai leading various tribes' troops making rebellion; Xi'erjisi thrust body cutting rebel formations; dismounted hand-to-hand fighting; rebel masses none not routed and collapsed.
translations.idiomatic: Under Ögedei he followed Tolui west. When the army halted at Jingzhao, Yilahudai led tribal troops in revolt; Xi'erjisi plunged into the rebel ranks, fought on foot, and swept the enemy aside.

sentences.zh: 俄失所乘馬，步走至睿宗軍中。

translations.literal: Suddenly lost his mounted horse; walked on foot reaching Ruizong's army center.
translations.idiomatic: He soon lost his horse and reached Tolui's camp on foot.

sentences.zh: 賊退，睿宗嘉其勤勞，妻以侍女唆火臺。

translations.literal: Rebels retreated; Ruizong praised his diligent labor; gave in marriage the maid Suo Huotai.
translations.idiomatic: When the rebels withdrew, Tolui praised his valor and gave him the maid Suo Huotai in marriage.

sentences.zh: 世祖尤愛之，軍旅田獵，未嘗不在左右。

translations.literal: Shizu especially favored him; on marches and hunts, never once not at left and right.
translations.idiomatic: Kublai favored him above all; he was never far from the Khan on campaign or at the hunt.

sentences.zh: 初，昔兒吉思之妻為皇子乳母，於是皇太后待以家人之禮，得同飲白馬湩。

translations.literal: At first, Xi'erjisi's wife was crown prince's wet nurse; therefore the Empress Dowager treated with family rites; permitted to drink together white horse kumiss.
translations.idiomatic: Because Xi'erjisi's wife had been wet nurse to the crown prince, the Empress Dowager treated them as kin and allowed them to share the white mare's milk—a privilege reserved for the closest of kin.

sentences.zh: 時朝廷舊典，白馬湩非宗戚貴胄不得飲也。

translations.literal: At that time the court's old statute: white horse kumiss, not imperial kin and noble lineage may not drink.
translations.idiomatic: By court custom, only imperial kin and the highest nobility might drink white mare's milk.

sentences.zh: 昔兒吉思子塔出，為寶兒赤、叠只斡耳朵千戶。

translations.literal: Xi'erjisi's son Taqo, served as ba'urchi, and Dieji Ordo chiliarch.
translations.idiomatic: Xi'erjisi's son Taqo served as a royal attendant and chiliarch of Dieji Ordo.

sentences.zh: 塔出子千家奴、撒裏蠻。

translations.literal: Taqo's sons Qianjianu and Sariman.
translations.idiomatic: Taqo's sons were Qianjianu and Sariman.

sentences.zh: 千家奴從征乃顏，力戰而死，帝命籍乃顏人口、財物以賜之。

translations.literal: Qianjianu followed campaigning against Nayan; fought vigorously and died; the Emperor ordered registering Nayan's population and goods and property to grant to them.
translations.idiomatic: Qianjianu died fighting Nayan; the Khan ordered Nayan's subjects and goods registered and granted to the family.

sentences.zh: 撒裏蠻年十六，從世祖討阿裏不哥，戰於失門禿，有功，賜號拔都兒，賞賚尤厚，授光祿少卿，仍襲為叠只斡耳朵千戶，改同僉宣徽院，進僉院事。

translations.literal: Sariman age sixteen; followed Shizu suppressing Ariq Böke; battled at Shimentu; had merit; granted title Badur; rewards especially thick; appointed Vice Director of Splendid Happiness; still inherited as Dieji Ordo chiliarch; changed to Associate Director of the Palace Administration; promoted to Director of the Office.
translations.idiomatic: At sixteen Sariman followed Kublai against Ariq Böke, fought at Shimentu with distinction, and was granted the title Badur ("Hero") with rich reward. He became Vice Director of Splendid Happiness, succeeded to the Dieji Ordo chiliarchy, and rose through the Palace Administration to its directorship.

sentences.zh: 以管軍千戶從征乃顏有功，賞金盞二、金五十兩，復入為同知宣徽院事。

translations.literal: As army-administering chiliarch followed campaigning against Nayan with merit; rewarded two gold cups and fifty liang gold; again entered as Associate Director of Palace Administration.
translations.idiomatic: Leading his chiliarchy against Nayan he was rewarded with two gold cups and fifty taels of gold, and reappointed associate director of the Palace Administration.

sentences.zh: 成宗時，拜宣徽使，加大司徒，卒。

translations.literal: In Chengzong's time, appointed Palace Administration commissioner; added Grand Steward; died.
translations.idiomatic: Under Chengzong he became palace administration commissioner and Grand Steward, and died in office.

sentences.zh: 子帖木叠兒襲為叠只斡耳朵千戶，累遷宣徽院使，遙授左丞相。

translations.literal: Son Temür-Ochir inherited as Dieji Ordo chiliarch; repeatedly promoted to Palace Administration commissioner; remotely granted left chancellor.
translations.idiomatic: His son Temür-Ochir succeeded to the Dieji Ordo chiliarchy, rose to head the Palace Administration, and was given the honorary title of left chancellor.

sentences.zh: ○哈散納

translations.literal: ○ Hasanna
translations.idiomatic: ○ Hasanna
